title: Figment to Support Staking Through BNY’s Digital Asset Custody Platform
summary: Figment will support BNY's staking offering through its validator infrastructure, giving eligible institutions a route from custody into protocol participation.
content:
TL;DR

  • Figment will provide validator infrastructure for BNY's institutional staking offering.
  • Eligible clients would access staking within the bank's digital asset custody service.
  • The arrangement adds operational infrastructure without removing token-price or validator risks.

BNY’s digital asset custody business is adding another route into staking through a collaboration with Figment. The development addresses a practical institutional problem: earning protocol rewards while keeping assets within an established custody and reporting relationship.

In its November 12 announcement, Figment said its validators would support BNY’s staking offering for eligible clients. The release names asset managers, ETF issuers, corporations and wealth managers among the potential users, without providing a launch date or a universal list of eligible accounts.

Custody and validator operations play different roles

The arrangement combines BNY’s custody and servicing framework with Figment’s infrastructure for participating in blockchain validation. That allows the two providers to supply different parts of one client workflow.

Holding an asset safely and using it in a protocol are related responsibilities, but they require different operations. Custody focuses on control, safekeeping and administration. Validator infrastructure performs the continuing network duties that can generate staking rewards.

For a large investment firm, integration can reduce the number of separate processes its staff must coordinate. Reconciliation, permissions and reporting still need to work across the whole arrangement, however. A convenient interface does not make those responsibilities disappear; it gives the providers a defined place to organize them.

This builds on an existing custody strategy

BNY had already outlined a staking collaboration with Galaxy in an August 4 announcement. That release described an integrated institutional service and said the offering and related infrastructure enhancements were subject to regulatory review.

The Figment announcement therefore should not be framed as BNY discovering staking for the first time. It is another development in the infrastructure supporting a previously stated direction.

NewsBTC’s coverage of BNY’s European custody expansion under MiCA provides a second part of that history. Geographic permissions, supported assets and individual client eligibility remain specific to the relevant service and entity.

Protocol rewards are not a guaranteed return

Ethereum’s staking documentation explains that validators receive rewards for performing network duties. Downtime can lead to missed rewards and penalties, while certain forms of misconduct can cause slashing. Using a provider adds operational and counterparty considerations to that protocol exposure.

The economic distinction is straightforward. A holder can accumulate more units of an asset while the value of the position falls in dollars. Staking income and market-price performance are different components of the final result.

NewsBTC examined that distinction in its report on Sygnum’s ETH-denominated investment fund. That fund includes separate trading strategies, so its target should not be imported into the BNY service as though it were a quoted staking rate.

Institutional demand has to become measurable use

The potential benefit is an easier operational route for institutions that already hold supported digital assets with a custodian. That could matter to firms whose investment policy allows staking but whose internal processes make managing validators directly impractical.

Actual adoption would need to be judged through live availability, assets staked, service performance and the terms clients receive. Fees, exit arrangements, reporting quality and responsibility for operational losses would all affect the proposition, even if the underlying protocol reward were identical.

The announcement does not disclose those commercial details or a guaranteed level of participation. It establishes the collaboration and the intended access model. Delivering a service that institutions can use consistently, within their own mandates and liquidity needs, is the next practical test.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Upbit’s $40 Billion Crypto Custody Empire Faces Shrinking Deposits
summary: South Korean cryptocurrency heavyweight Dunamu, the parent company of Upbit, disclosed approximately $41.5 billion in customer-held digital assets as deposit liabilities contracted 32.2%. The financial disclosures reveal mounting pressure on the country’s largest cryptocurrency exchange operator, ev...
content:
South Korean cryptocurrency heavyweight Dunamu, the parent company of Upbit, disclosed approximately $41.5 billion in customer-held digital assets as deposit liabilities contracted 32.2%. The financial disclosures reveal mounting pressure on the country’s largest cryptocurrency exchange operator, even as its standalone business remains profitable.

Key Takeaways

  • Upbit’s customer cryptocurrency holdings declined to 55.46 trillion won ($41.54 billion), reflecting a 10.9% reduction in reported value.
  • Customer deposit liabilities contracted 32.2% to 3.92 trillion won ($2.94 billion).
  • Dunamu reported an 18.58 billion won ($13.92 million) consolidated quarterly loss despite profitable standalone operations.

Upbit’s $41.5 Billion Crypto Holdings Reveal a Growing Financial Divide

According to Dunamu’s quarterly regulatory filing published Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, customer-entrusted cryptocurrency holdings totaled 55.46 trillion won ($41.54 billion) as of Sept. 30, compared with 62.23 trillion won ($46.62 billion) at the end of 2025.

The difference represents a 6.78 trillion won ($5.08 billion) reduction in reported asset values. However, the decline does not necessarily indicate equivalent customer withdrawals, since fluctuations in cryptocurrency prices can materially influence custody valuations.

More strikingly, customer deposit liabilities fell from 5.78 trillion won ($4.33 billion) to 3.92 trillion won ($2.94 billion), representing a 32.2% contraction. Despite these reductions, Upbit’s custody business remains substantial. Customer holdings included 175,473 BTC, valued at approximately 19.97 trillion won ($14.96 billion), alongside 6.4 billion XRP worth 13.03 trillion won ($9.76 billion).

The earnings report says the platform also maintained 2.27 million ethereum (ETH) valued at 8.24 trillion won ($6.18 billion), plus considerable solana (SOL) and dogecoin (DOGE) holdings. Separately, Dunamu disclosed proprietary reserves of 16,585 BTC worth 1.89 trillion won ($1.41 billion).

Why Is Upbit’s Parent Losing Money Despite a Profitable Core Business?

Beyond shrinking customer balances, Dunamu’s financial statements reveal a pronounced earnings deterioration. Third-quarter consolidated revenue declined 60.7% to 151.7 billion won ($113.65 million), compared with 385.86 billion won ($289.06 million) during the corresponding quarter in 2025.

Meanwhile, operating expenses increased to 155.23 billion won ($116.29 million), producing a 3.53 billion won ($2.65 million) operating loss. Consolidated net earnings reversed from a 239.04 billion won ($179.08 million) profit to an 18.58 billion won ($13.92 million) loss.

Yet Dunamu’s standalone business remained profitable, generating 14.17 billion won ($10.62 million) in quarterly net income. Subsidiary performance and broader financial expenses consequently weighed heavily on consolidated results. Third-quarter finance costs reached 53.14 billion won ($39.81 million), including interest expenses, financial instrument valuation losses and foreign exchange adjustments.

For the first nine months of 2026, consolidated revenue declined 52.9% to 559.78 billion won ($419.36 million), while net profit fell 86.3% to 89.84 billion won ($67.30 million). Nevertheless, Dunamu retained 5.96 trillion won ($4.46 billion) in consolidated equity.

The disclosures illustrate a widening distinction between Upbit’s profitable core operations and its parent company’s deteriorating consolidated performance. The centralized exchange (CEX) platform’s performance is particularly intriguing when viewed through the lens of its geographic position relative to competing exchanges.

Although its custody business remains enormous, declining customer balances and contracting trading revenue present an increasingly difficult financial equation for South Korea’s dominant cryptocurrency exchange operator.

title: Invesco Bitcoin ETF Adds BNY Mellon Custody While Keeping Coinbase Arrangement
summary: The Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF has signed a BNY Mellon custody agreement while retaining Coinbase, adding infrastructure without disclosing asset transfers.
content:
TL;DR

  • Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF disclosed a new BNY Mellon custody agreement in a November 12 SEC filing.
  • The agreement took effect November 6, and the existing Coinbase arrangement remains in place.
  • The filing expands custody infrastructure without quantifying any Bitcoin transferred to the new provider.

The Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF has added a major banking name to the arrangements supporting its Bitcoin holdings. A November 12 securities filing discloses a custody agreement with The Bank of New York Mellon, while retaining the trust’s existing relationship with Coinbase.

The development is about how an established fund safeguards assets. It does not announce a new ETF or a fresh Bitcoin purchase. For institutions evaluating crypto exposure, however, the number and identity of available custodians can matter well beyond a fund’s headline fee.

BNY joins the fund’s custody arrangements

The Form 8-K says the agreement began on November 6 and has an initial five-year term, subject to its termination provisions. Invesco, the sponsor, anticipates using both BNY Mellon and Coinbase to custody the trust’s Bitcoin.

BNY will maintain segregated custody accounts on its books for the fund’s assets. The filing does not state how much Bitcoin had been transferred to the bank or how the holdings would be divided between providers. Those are separate operational questions from signing the contract.

Keeping the earlier arrangement creates the possibility of using more than one provider. It should not be read as evidence that Coinbase has been replaced or that every coin now sits within BNY’s custody system.

The contract defines what protection actually means

The custody agreement requires commercially reasonable insurance and sets a standard of care for BNY’s work. It also contains liability limits and exclusions. Its terms say the digital assets are not deposits covered by federal deposit insurance.

That distinction deserves attention whenever a bank enters crypto custody. Safekeeping involves controls over access, records and instructions; it does not remove Bitcoin’s market-price risk. An insurance requirement is also different from a blanket promise that every possible loss will be reimbursed.

For fund oversight teams, the practical work includes understanding who can authorise transfers, how holdings are reconciled and what happens if a service becomes unavailable. A familiar banking name does not make those operational details unnecessary.

Bank custody is expanding across several markets

BNY’s wider digital-asset custody platform dates to 2022. In an October 8 announcement, the bank described an expansion for selected institutions in the European Union under MiCA. That European development involves its regional entity and is separate from this US fund agreement.

The broader direction is nevertheless clear: established financial-service providers are building infrastructure for institutions that want crypto exposure within familiar operating frameworks. The work includes custody, administration and transfer processes, rather than simply placing a buy button next to Bitcoin.

NewsBTC’s reporting on Bitget’s open custody network reflects another version of this demand. Institutions increasingly have choices about how trading access and asset storage fit together.

More providers change operations before they change demand

A second custody relationship can offer a fund another route for storing and moving assets. Whether it reduces concentration in practice depends on how the sponsor allocates holdings and manages dependencies. Two signed agreements alone do not establish how much redundancy exists in day-to-day operations. The sponsor would still need to reconcile balances across providers, coordinate transfer instructions and ensure that its valuation and reporting systems account for the same assets.

The market-demand question is different. NewsBTC’s report on recent Bitcoin ETF redemptions concerns investors changing exposure. A custody contract describes the infrastructure behind that exposure. The two developments can occur at the same time without contradicting one another.

For BTCO, the next meaningful disclosures would clarify implementation, asset allocation and any material changes to fund expenses. The present filing establishes an additional banking relationship while leaving the existing Coinbase arrangement intact.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Trezor customer data exposed in 3rd partner breach this year
summary: Trezor warned an attacker has been able to access customer names, phone numbers and delivery addresses linked to 27,000 orders from one of its shipping providers.
content:
Hardware wallet maker Trezor has disclosed its third partner data breach this year, warning that an attacker accessed personal information linked to approximately 27,000 orders held by shipping provider Skladon.

The exposed information includes customers’ names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses and purchase details for orders placed between Aug. 9 and Nov. 7.

Trezor said Monday that it believes the attacker exported the data. Its own systems were not compromised, and customers’ devices remain secure, the company said.

The disclosure follows an August breach at shipping provider ShipMonk that initially affected about 13,700 customers. Trezor later said another approximately 67,000 US customers were affected, including people whose records ShipMonk had assured it were deleted.

In September, a separate breach at marketing platform Brevo exposed 347,149 email addresses from Trezor’s newsletter list.

“Treat any unexpected call, text, email or letter about your order as suspicious, and be alert to potential risks to your physical security,” the company said on X. “Trezor will never cold-call you or ask for your wallet backup.”

The disclosure came as Trezor launched its anonymous pickup service in 18 European countries, allowing customers to order devices without giving out home addresses.

“For crypto holders, a leaked shipping record does more harm than most. It links a person, a home address and the fact that they own crypto,” it said.

title: Bitcoin Whales Sit on Record $8 Billion Losses—but They Aren’t Selling
summary: Bitcoin’s short-term whale cohort is sitting on nearly $8 billion in unrealized losses, the highest level on record, after a roughly 30% correction since October. Yet exchange inflows remain relatively contained, suggesting large recent buyers have not rushed to capitulate.   Bitcoin’s Recent Buyers...
content:
Bitcoin’s short-term whale cohort is sitting on nearly $8 billion in unrealized losses, the highest level on record, after a roughly 30% correction since October. Yet exchange inflows remain relatively contained, suggesting large recent buyers have not rushed to capitulate.

Key Takeaways

  • Short-term bitcoin whales hold nearly $8 billion in unrealized losses after a roughly 30% correction.
  • Binance whale inflows remain contained, suggesting large recent buyers have not capitulated.
  • Holding $60K-$63K could keep pressure manageable; losing it may force more whales toward exchanges.

Bitcoin’s Recent Buyers Face First Major Stress Test

Bitcoin’s newest large holders are under more pressure than ever, but they are not yet behaving like a cohort in panic.

Short-term holder whales that accumulated BTC within the past 155 days are now carrying close to $8 billion in unrealized losses, according to Cryptoquant market analyst Darkfost.

The figure is a record for the cohort and follows a sharp reversal in bitcoin’s price. BTC had rallied more than 51% from June before entering a correction of nearly 30% from its October levels.

Bitcoin was recently trading around $64,800, back above a closely watched “pain zone” between $60,000 and $63,000 after briefly touching its largest loss cluster over the weekend.

Record Losses, but No Rush for the Exit

The headline number is severe. What matters more is what whales are doing with those losses.

Darkfost said monthly average whale inflows to Binance have risen from roughly 1,200 BTC to 2,100 BTC. Some daily spikes have exceeded 4,000 to 5,000 BTC, while Nov. 3 saw a sharper jump above 9,000 BTC.

Even so, those flows remain below levels recorded in June and February 2026, despite the much larger paper losses now held by the cohort.

That gap suggests many recent whales are choosing to sit through the drawdown rather than move aggressively toward exchanges.

Recent Buyers Face Their First Major Stress Test

Short-term whales are especially important because they entered during bitcoin’s latest expansion phase. Many likely bought as momentum accelerated and the fear of missing a sustained breakout grew. That leaves them more exposed than long-term holders with far lower cost bases.

If these investors begin sending significantly more BTC to exchanges, then selling pressure could intensify quickly. So far, that has not happened. The current pattern points to stress without full capitulation, a distinction that could shape bitcoin’s next move.

The $60,000-$63,000 Zone Becomes Critical

Bitcoin’s ability to stay above the $60,000 to $63,000 area now carries added significance.

A sustained break below that region could deepen unrealized losses and test the conviction of whales that entered over the past several months. Holding above it, by contrast, may give the market time to absorb the correction.

There is one important caveat. Darkfost said the $8 billion loss estimate could include some activity linked to the Binance hack or UTXO consolidations, which may distort the cohort data.

Even with that limitation, the signal is striking. Recent bitcoin whales are carrying record pain. For now, they are mostly choosing not to sell it.

title: PowerCompute Orders 600 New Bitcoin Miners as Higher Output Meets Lower Revenue
summary: PowerCompute plans to replace older machines with 600 new Bitcoin miners after Q3 production rose while revenue declined.
content:
TL;DR

  • PowerCompute mined 23.9 BTC in Q3, but lower average Bitcoin prices reduced revenue.
  • A roughly $1 million purchase of 600 replacement miners targets about 10% more active hashrate by mid-December.
  • The operating loss and going-concern disclosure remain relevant alongside improved mining margins.

Producing more Bitcoin does not necessarily mean bringing in more dollars. PowerCompute’s latest quarterly results demonstrate that tension, while a new equipment order shows how the small US miner intends to improve output without building another power-hungry site.

The company reported higher Bitcoin production but lower revenue for the quarter ended September 30. It also disclosed a cash purchase of replacement machines that it expects to lift active hashrate by about 10%. The practical question is whether that additional computing work can earn enough to cover the equipment and the rest of the business.

Bitcoin production and revenue moved in opposite directions

In its November 13 results release, PowerCompute reported mining 23.9 BTC, up 35.8% from a year earlier. Revenue fell to approximately $1.9 million from $2.2 million as the average value of coins produced declined. Its stated mining margin improved to 50.7%, compared with 29% in the preceding quarter.

These measures answer different questions. Coin production describes the output of the mining operation. Revenue converts that production into dollars at the applicable values. Mining margin then considers a narrower set of operating costs; it does not automatically cover every salary, professional fee or equipment charge across the company.

A miner can improve at running machines and still struggle to generate a sustainable company-wide profit. Looking at all three measures makes that distinction visible.

The new machines replace equipment already on site

The new order comprises 600 Antminer S21++ units costing about $1 million, with deployment expected by mid-December. PowerCompute says replacing older machines at its Mississippi facility should add roughly 80–85 petahashes per second without additional power capacity. That is a management estimate, dependent on delivery and installation.

The attraction of a replacement programme is straightforward: it tries to squeeze more useful computation from an existing electrical connection. It can avoid some of the construction and interconnection work involved in adding an entirely new site. Installation still means downtime, and the advertised performance has to survive ordinary operating conditions.

Paying cash also puts the economic test close to home. The investment needs to justify money that could otherwise support operating expenses or remain available for unexpected repairs.

Efficiency matters as much as the machine count

PowerCompute’s September fleet-refresh announcement described an earlier generation of replacements that used about 21.5 joules per terahash, compared with roughly 34 for retired equipment. Those figures concern that earlier programme, rather than the newly ordered S21++ units.

The comparison explains why raw machine counts can mislead. Two fleets containing the same number of devices can consume different amounts of power and perform very different amounts of hashing. The relevant calculation combines electricity prices, actual efficiency, uptime and the share of the network’s work each miner contributes.

NewsBTC’s coverage of PowerCompute’s earlier debt repayment and production update also showed the role of curtailment. Sometimes selling or conserving electricity can be more attractive than running every machine continuously.

Improved mining results leave a wider financial test

The latest release still reported an operating loss of about $0.9 million despite net income near $0.4 million, and it referenced substantial doubt about the company’s ability to continue as a going concern. Those disclosures deserve attention alongside the better mining margin.

NewsBTC has covered other miners directing capital toward AI infrastructure. PowerCompute’s immediate equipment decision takes a different practical route: improve the Bitcoin output of power and sites it already operates.

The next useful checkpoints are delivered machines, sustained hashrate and cash generated after the upgrade. A larger production figure will be encouraging only if it comes with acceptable costs and enough liquidity to keep the operation running.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

About Hyperliquid Crypto Project and Team

Hyperliquid is a DEX designed to combine the speed and user experience of CEXs with the transparency and security of DeFi. Jeff Yan has expertise in quantitative trading, while Iliensinc, though pseudonymous, is highly respected for his skills in blockchain infrastructure.

The team also includes members from prestigious institutions, such as Caltech and MIT, as well as professionals from top firms like Citadel and Hudson River Trading. The project prioritizes community, which is reflected in their rejection of venture capital funding, allocating 70% of its tokens to users, and the redistribution of all revenue back to the community.

Key Features of Hyperliquid Crypto Exchange

The key features of Hyperliquid crypto exchange are an on-chain order book, gas-free transactions, high leverage trading, liquidity vaults, cross-chain compatibility, and pro-level trading tools.

On-Chain Order Book

Most decentralized exchanges use off-chain order books or automated market makers due to the high throughput required by on-chain order books. However, the platform runs its order book on-chain, providing transparency, security, and speed-optimized transactions through its custom consensus mechanism, HyperBFT, which can confirm up to 200,000 transactions per second using Byzantine Fault Tolerance.

Gas-Free Transactions

Since Hyperliquid operates on its own Layer 1 chain, it controls the entire infrastructure and does not require users to pay gas fees for transactions, unlike Ethereum or other public blockchains. Instead, the platform covers the underlying transaction costs internally and charges users only minimal fees.

High Leverage Trading

Hyperliquid offers up to 40x leverage on perpetual futures contracts, allowing traders to amplify their positions beyond what their actual trading capital can carry. Due to the high risk associated with leverage trading, this feature is particularly tailored to experienced traders who are familiar with the strategy and want to increase their profit potential from rapid market movements.

Liquidity Vaults

Liquidity vaults on Hyperliquid are created by individuals or entities who want to share their trading strategies with others. Users can deposit funds into these vaults and earn a share of the profits or losses based on the vault leader’s trading performance. Aside from user-owned vaults, the Hyperliquid platform features protocol vaults, such as the Hyperliquidity Provider (HLP) Vault, which acts as a market maker and liquidation mechanism, earning a portion of the trading fees.

Cross-Chain Compatibility

Previously, users had to bridge into Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid. This integration eliminates the previous process that required traders to bridge funds through Arbitrum before accessing Hyperliquid.

Pro-level Trading Tools

Another standout feature of Hyperliquid is the advanced trading tools available to traders, which are similar to those used by professional traders on traditional exchanges. This includes features such as the on-chain order book, real-time charts, customizable order types (including limit, market, and stop orders), in-depth market data, and responsive user interfaces, catering to both retail and institutional traders.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Hyperliquid?

The pros of Hyperliquid are listed below:

  • Advanced Trading Features: Hyperliquid offers a wide range of trading options, including spot trading, perpetual trading, pre-launch futures contracts, margin trading, and up to 40x leverage. Additionally, it supports multiple order types, including market, limit, stop market, stop limit, scale, and TWAP orders, providing traders with advanced tools to execute various strategies.
  • Community-Owned Liquidity Pools (Vaults): The Hyperliquid platform features an advanced vault system, where users can open their own vaults or contribute deposits to existing ones, sharing in the profits (about 10%).
  • Fast Transactions on a Custom Layer 1 Blockchain: Hyperliquid operates on its own Layer 1 blockchain, utilizing a proprietary HyperBFT proof-of-stake consensus that enables up to 200,000 transactions per second, with near-instant finality and very low latency.
  • Low Fees and No Gas Charges on Trades: Thanks to its PoS consensus and efficient design, Hyperliquid charges very low maker (0.045%) and taker (0.015%) fees and eliminates gas fees for trading transactions, significantly reducing trading costs compared to most other decentralized exchanges.
  • Broad Asset Support and Cross-Chain Bridging: The platform supports over 100 assets, including major cryptocurrencies like BTC, ETH, AVAX, SOL, and SUI. It also offers multiple bridges (Arbitrum Bridge, Synapse, HyBridge) to facilitate cross-chain transfers, enhancing liquidity and user flexibility.
  • User-Friendly Experience with One-Click Trading: The Hyperliquid decentralized perpetual exchange simplifies trading with one-click order execution and wallet connection. This helps to avoid repeated confirmations and streamlines the trading experience, similar to centralized platforms.
  • Governance and Community Focus: The native HYPE token enables governance participation and incentivizes trading activity. The platform is community-oriented, rejecting venture capital funding and reinvesting profits in users, which solidifies a more user-focused ecosystem.

The cons of Hyperliquid are listed below:

  • Limited Withdrawal Options: Currently, USDC is the primary cryptocurrency supported for withdrawals. If you wish to withdraw another cryptocurrency or stablecoin from Hyperliquid, you will first need to convert it to USDC. 
  • Centralization: Although Hyperliquid claims to be fully decentralized, some have criticized Hyperliquid for its relatively centralized structure. Critics argue that the protocol is not truly decentralized in comparison to other Layer-1 blockchain networks like Ethereum. 
  • Systemic Risk and Operational Concerns: The platform has faced criticism over incidents such as the JELLY token controversy, where a large trader’s actions resulted in substantial losses for liquidity providers. Critics argue that mixed vaults expose users to systemic risk and that unrestricted position sizes allow potential manipulation.

title: FBI Seizes 900+ Webcam Videos in $400M North Korean Crypto Crime Scheme
summary: North Korean hackers used stolen webcam recordings to impersonate trusted contacts in a scheme linked to more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft. The FBI seized over 900 videos as authorities disrupted infrastructure supporting the operation. Stolen Faces Helped Hackers Win Trust The Federal ...
content:
North Korean hackers used stolen webcam recordings to impersonate trusted contacts in a scheme linked to more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft. The FBI seized over 900 videos as authorities disrupted infrastructure supporting the operation.

Key Takeaways

  • Fake meeting updates tricked targets into installing malicious software.
  • Attackers sometimes waited over a year for wallet balances to increase.
  • A targeted software library received tens of millions of weekly downloads.

Stolen Faces Helped Hackers Win Trust

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warned on Nov. 12 that North Korean hackers used secretly recorded webcam videos to impersonate trusted contacts through a scheme called FaceStealer. The bureau stated:

“Using the FaceStealer scheme, the actors have stolen more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the past 18 months and attempted to compromise the open-source software supply chain.”

The U.S. Justice Department (DOJ) announced the same day that it had disrupted cloud-based infrastructure used by the North Korean hackers. Under a federal warrant, the FBI also seized more than 900 webcam videos of FaceStealer victims. The department said the hackers target cryptocurrency industry workers and have increasingly gone after maintainers, the people who develop and maintain open-source software.

Hackers invited targets to fake video meetings using stolen or fabricated accounts on platforms including Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack, and Discord. They read chat histories from compromised accounts to write messages that appeared to come from someone the target knew. During the meeting, they played stolen webcam recordings of familiar contacts, often adding extra videos so the call appeared to include several participants.

Fake Audio Fixes Opened Computers to Theft

Describing the FaceStealer impersonation scheme, the FBI explained:

“FaceStealer relies on imposter versions of popular video meetings like Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meets controlled by the hackers.”

A fabricated technical problem prompted requests to install an update, run a script, or paste commands into a terminal.

When targets followed the fake troubleshooting instructions, they installed malware that recorded what they typed, captured images of their screens, and allowed attackers to keep accessing their computers. The hackers also saved webcam footage and contact lists to impersonate those victims in future scams. In some cases, attackers monitored victims’ cryptocurrency wallets for months or more than a year, waiting for balances to grow before stealing the funds.

Google researchers previously documented malware delivered through programming tests and meeting software in a separate North Korean campaign using public blockchains to conceal malicious code. FaceStealer predominantly relied on genuine victim recordings, the FBI said. Attackers had also begun creating deepfakes, digitally fabricated videos depicting influential industry figures.

Software Accounts Put More Users at Risk

The FBI described a compromised maintainer whose JavaScript library, a collection of reusable code, received tens of millions of weekly downloads. Attackers used that access to create malicious software components. Rapid detection and response prevented potentially widespread harm.

In a separate campaign disclosed by authorities in September, North Korean hackers posed as recruiters and asked job applicants to complete fake technical interviews and coding assessments. Developers and cryptocurrency specialists were instructed to download files presented as coding tests or tools to fix video calls. Those files installed malware, infecting at least 30,000 devices across 100 countries.

A similar recruiter ploy helped attackers infiltrate crypto exchange Binance before its Oct. 29 hack, which saw approximately $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from the exchange’s wallets. Binance said one of its engineers, approached by someone posing as a recruiter, was told to download a coding assignment containing malware onto a work computer.

Protection against impersonation and counterfeit websites includes verifying requests independently. The FBI recommended joining meetings through official applications with an invite code, and avoiding scripts or terminal commands presented as updates. Suspected victims were advised to secure funds using a new wallet on an unaffected device and notify contacts and employers.

title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Falls 9.13%, Giving Active Miners Some Breathing Room
summary: Bitcoin’s November 14 difficulty reduction improves expected mining output per hash, while power costs and dollar prices remain decisive.
content:
TL;DR

  • Bitcoin difficulty fell to approximately 134.82 trillion at block 975,744 on November 14.
  • The 9.13% reduction improves the expected return from each hash, with other conditions unchanged.
  • Power costs, fees and Bitcoin’s dollar price still determine whether individual operations are profitable.

Bitcoin’s automatic difficulty adjustment has made the next block easier for miners to find. At block 975,744 on November 14, the network reduced difficulty by approximately 9.13%, bringing the measure to 134.82 trillion.

That offers some relief to operators whose machines remain online. It also needs to be read correctly: the network has changed the amount of computational work expected for a successful block, not the electricity bill on a particular mining site or the price a miner receives when selling Bitcoin.

The adjustment responds to the previous mining period

Mempool’s network data records the new difficulty at 134,823,837,323,272.7, compared with 148,364,561,003,867.4 previously. The adjustment block’s recorded time was 05:02:50 UTC on November 14. October 29’s adjustment had increased difficulty, so the latest move reverses part of that earlier tightening.

Bitcoin’s developer documentation explains the mechanism: the network retargets every 2,016 blocks, using the elapsed time across the preceding period to steer block production back toward its intended pace. Slower production leads to an easier target; faster production leads to a harder one.

The setting is therefore backward-looking. It summarises block production over an interval rather than identifying a specific company, outage or price move responsible for a change in mining activity.

The benefit per hash is slightly larger than the headline cut

Difficulty and expected success per hash move inversely. Dividing the previous difficulty by the new one gives approximately 1.1004. In other words, the same amount of hashing now has roughly a 10% higher expected success rate than before, assuming the relevant reward and other conditions remain unchanged.

That is a calculation from the published difficulty values, not a promise that every miner will produce 10% more coins in its next reporting period. Mining outcomes vary, pool payout methods differ and individual machines experience downtime. The improvement describes expected work efficiency at the protocol level.

A fleet upgrade is another way to change the calculation. NewsBTC’s earlier PowerCompute production report illustrates how operators also manage equipment, financing and power use alongside network conditions.

Dollar revenue can still fall as mining gets easier

Consider a simplified example with fees and uptime held constant. If difficulty falls about 9.13% while Bitcoin’s dollar price also falls about 9.13%, the higher expected Bitcoin output per hash is broadly offset by the lower value of each coin. The percentage effects work through a ratio, rather than adding neatly together.

Real operations are more complicated. Electricity contracts, cooling, maintenance and financing can change the break-even point. Transaction fees also vary, affecting the reward available for the work performed. A miner with efficient equipment and cheap power can face very different economics from another running older machines.

That explains why an easier network does not automatically stop industry restructuring. As NewsBTC’s coverage of Hut 8’s AI-campus plans shows, companies may compare mining against other uses of their power and capital.

The next period will test how miners respond

The Bitcoin Core implementation applies retargeting at defined block intervals. Between those points, the difficulty setting persists even while the amount of active mining equipment changes.

If improved economics encourage machines to return, blocks may arrive faster and put upward pressure on the following adjustment. If more capacity leaves, the opposite can happen. Estimates for that next change will shift as new blocks arrive; they should not be treated as completed adjustments.

The confirmed development is narrower and more useful: the November 14 cut reduces expected work per block for the current period. Whether that becomes lasting financial relief depends on the prices and costs miners face while using it.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Hackers inject credit card, crypto-stealing malware into 178 major websites
summary: Ledger and Coinpass were among the businesses whose websites served malware designed to steal visitors’ crypto and credit card details, according to security researchers.
content:
Update (Nov. 17 at 4:43 am UTC): This article has been updated to include a statement from Salesforce and analysis of the stolen funds by Galaxy Digital’s Alex Thorn.

Major global brands including Ledger, Salesforce and BBC served cryptocurrency and credit card-stealing malware to website visitors on Monday, according to security researchers, the latest in a wave of wide-reaching cyberattacks.

Dubbed “Optimjack” by researcher Amirul Iman, the campaign delivered malicious code through website scripts, including those hosted by Optimizely, a website optimization platform. The malware can replace legitimate cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled alternatives when visitors copy addresses. It also captured credit card details entered into website forms, according to a separate analysis by cybersecurity firm StepSecurity.

The campaign affected website scripts belonging to 178 organizations, including hardware wallet Ledger, OANDA / Coinpass and trading platforms IG, Interactive Investor and TMS Brokers, according to Report URI’s investigation. 

Other affected brands included IKEA, Salesforce, Zoom, the BBC and CNN — websites that collectively attract millions of visitors a day. 

A spokesperson for Optimizely confirmed to Cointelegraph on Monday that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects.

“We have blocked access to the vulnerable path and deployed a fix,” they said. “We have removed the injected code from affected projects. We have also ended active sessions, revoked tokens, and reset access for affected user accounts. Finally, we have blocked any code from being delivered in Cloudflare,” they said, adding that they’re continuing to investigate and have notified all affected customers.

BBC was among the first websites seen serving the Optimizely injection at 4:21 am UTC on Monday, according to Report URI CEO Scott Helme. By 9:52 pm UTC, most of the malicious code across the 187 websites had been removed, with Ledger’s snippet cleaned at about 8:41 pm UTC. 

Cointelegraph reached out to Ledger, Coinpass, and a number of other major businesses reported as impacted by the malicious injection. 

A spokesperson for Salesforce told Cointelegraph it was investigating unauthorized modifications to Optimizely scripts used on certain Salesforce websites.

“As a precaution, Salesforce is confirming Optimizely scripts are disabled across preview and production instances.”

How trusted websites served a theft tool

Optimizely lets businesses run experiments and custom code on their websites through JavaScript snippets. Attackers inserted malicious code into those customer projects, causing otherwise legitimate scripts to load the malware when visitors opened affected pages.

Once loaded, the malware could replace legitimate cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled alternatives, including addresses copied to a visitor’s clipboard. A user could then unknowingly paste the attacker’s address when making a transfer.

Related: PHP flaw draws millions of exploit attempts, Cloudflare CEO warns

The script also watched for credit card numbers, expiry dates and security codes entered into website forms and sent captured details to an attacker-controlled server. However, it could not read payment fields isolated inside third-party payment providers’ cross-origin frames, StepSecurity said.

Visitors using iPhones and iPads also faced an additional threat: the malicious script loaded code linked to the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits, according to Helme.

Researchers have yet to establish how attackers obtained access to modify the Optimizely projects.

Crypto losses remain unconfirmed

Despite the widespread attack, crypto addresses identified as linked to the malware received only around $7,100 in cryptocurrency on Monday, according to blockchain records checked by Cointelegraph. 

StepSecurity’s separate analysis put funds received or held across the wallets at roughly $6,600, noting that some addresses had activity predating the attack.

Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy Digital, estimated that victims have only sent around $2,300 in total to the addresses. In an analysis posted on X, Thorn said most of the Bitcoin receipts appeared to be the attacker’s own funds routed through an exchange back to their wallet, rather than proceeds from victims.

Helme said it could not determine how many payment card details or cookies had reached the attackers’ server. The skimmer could not read card details entered into payment providers’ cross-origin iframes, according to StepSecurity, potentially limiting its reach.

The campaign follows a string of recent threats to website security. In October, government agencies and other organizations took websites offline as a precaution over critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to take control of servers. Polymarket also temporarily suspended trading on Oct. 29 after a third-party provider was compromised, amid reports of users’ accounts being drained.

title: Russia Opens a Regulated Bitcoin Door on November 17—With a ₽300,000 Limit
summary: Russia’s approved crypto list takes effect on November 17, bringing Bitcoin, Ether and USDT into a regulated retail framework. The opening comes with tests, purchase limits and a crucial distinction between legal approval and actual trading.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH USDT

Russia’s approved crypto list takes effect on November 17, bringing Bitcoin, Ether and USDT into a regulated retail framework. The opening comes with tests, purchase limits and a crucial distinction between legal approval and actual trading.

Russia crypto rules taking effect on November 17 put Bitcoin, Ether and USDT on the approved list for non-qualified investors, marking a concrete step towards regulated retail access in one of cryptocurrency’s most politically complicated markets.

The Bank of Russia’s November 6 announcement allows purchases through intermediaries, subject to a ₽300,000 annual limit through each intermediary and an investor test. The date is a regulatory milestone, rather than proof that every broker or exchange has already opened its doors.

For the global market, the immediate question is how much usable access follows. A country approving crypto assets creates potential demand. It does not establish that the full permitted amount will be invested, or that Bitcoin’s price will respond.

What changes under the Russia crypto rules?

The central bank says the ordinance takes effect on November 17. Its notice states: “From that date, these assets may be publicly traded on exchanges.” The assets named are Bitcoin, Ether and USDT.

Non-qualified investors may use brokers, trust managers or crypto exchange offices in exchange and over-the-counter markets. The limit applies through a single intermediary, an important qualification when interpreting the cap.

Qualified investors have broader access without the same purchase restriction, but the notice says testing and acknowledgement of investment risks apply regardless of investor status. Permission therefore comes with an access process, rather than simply adding a buy button.

The regulator says selection considered liquidity, market capitalisation and at least five years of foreign-exchange pricing history. Inclusion is an eligibility decision; it is not a guarantee against losses.

Approval and a market launch are different dates

Interfax reported on November 6 that Moscow Exchange was targeting December 1 for cryptocurrency transactions and testing operations with professional participants. The report attributed the plan to senior managing director Boris Blokhin’s earlier comments.

That is a planned commercial launch, separate from the ordinance’s legal start. Readers should distinguish an asset being eligible for admission from a venue actually offering a functioning market to a particular customer.

The difference has practical consequences. A broker needs an available service, account arrangements and a way to settle transactions. A legal date does not demonstrate that all those steps have been completed for every participant.

Nor should a stated launch target be treated as a confirmed opening-day volume. The more informative evidence will be operating notices from venues, actual customer access and recorded trading after services begin.

The infrastructure has been taking shape

In an October 6 announcement, the Bank of Russia said it had admitted the first five digital depositories and four cryptocurrency exchange organisations under transitional provisions of the new framework.

The regulator described digital depositories as recording and transferring digital currencies and rights, while exchange organisations could buy and sell digital currencies on their own account outside organised trading.

Those functions help explain why this is more than an approved-coin list. A regulated market needs arrangements for holding, recording and moving investors’ rights as well as somewhere to agree a price.

For customers, the questions become familiar financial-service questions: who records the holding, how withdrawals work and what recourse exists if an intermediary fails. Regulatory recognition makes those questions more visible; it does not remove them.

Buying Bitcoin does not make it domestic payment money

The central bank’s July explanation of the broader law said the framework would take effect on September 1. It retained the prohibition on using cryptocurrency for payments inside Russia, while providing separately for exporters and importers to use it in cross-border transactions.

The distinction is central to the policy. An asset can be permitted for investment without becoming an accepted means of paying a domestic shop. Retail trading access and international commercial settlement belong to different parts of the framework.

It also prevents an investment announcement from being mistaken for an official endorsement of Bitcoin as a replacement for national money. The permissions concern specified activities, participants and channels.

For overseas observers, domestic permission is also only one part of the picture. A Russian rule cannot by itself determine a foreign provider’s eligibility requirements or willingness to serve a customer. The route available on paper and the route available in practice may differ.

How much new Bitcoin demand could follow?

The annual cap places a ceiling on an individual channel, but does not measure aggregate purchases. Estimating demand would require the number of eligible customers, their take-up rate and how much they actually allocate.

Some activity could also move from existing trading routes into the regulated system. In that scenario, higher reported domestic volume would not necessarily represent an equal amount of brand-new cryptocurrency demand worldwide.

BNC’s coverage of Bitcoin ETF flows illustrates why access and money flows need separate measurements. A market can have established investment products while investors are withdrawing capital.

The strongest follow-up indicators will be live market access, net purchases and reliable custody arrangements. November 17 supplies a clear legal milestone. What investors do with the new route will determine its market significance.

title: Harvard and Dartmouth Keep Bitcoin ETF Share Counts Steady as Q3 Values Rise
summary: Harvard and Dartmouth’s latest filings show stable Bitcoin ETF share counts, with higher quarter-end valuations and different choices elsewhere.
content:
TL;DR

  • Harvard and Dartmouth reported unchanged IBIT share counts between June and September quarter-ends.
  • Their September positions were worth about $144.1 million and $9.5 million respectively.
  • Harvard sharply increased its reported GLD share count, while Dartmouth also retained Ether and Solana fund positions.

Two university investment portfolios offer a quieter picture of institutional Bitcoin exposure than the usual buying-and-selling headlines. Harvard and Dartmouth reported the same numbers of shares in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of September as they had at the end of June. The positions became more valuable as the fund rose.

The distinction is useful: a larger dollar figure can describe a change in market prices without showing an increase in the number of shares held. These filings, submitted on November 13, also reveal other portfolio choices that put the Bitcoin positions into perspective.

The share counts stayed level at quarter-end

Harvard Management Company’s September filing lists 3,044,612 shares of the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, valued at $144.1 million. Dartmouth’s disclosure lists 201,531 shares worth approximately $9.5 million.

The corresponding June disclosures show identical share counts, valued at about $101.4 million and $6.7 million. That works out to an increase of roughly 42% in the reported value of each position. The calculation compares the two filing snapshots; it is not a measure of fresh cash invested during the quarter.

Matching endpoints do not establish that no transactions happened between them. A manager could trade during a quarter and finish with the same holding. The documents establish the reported balances on the two dates.

Harvard’s gold allocation shows a clearer change

The difference is easier to see in Harvard’s SPDR Gold Shares position. Its latest filing reports 1,161,000 GLD shares, compared with 58,862 in the June information table. That is nearly twenty times the earlier share count. The September position was worth about $442.2 million.

Those figures support a statement that Harvard’s reported exposure through that gold fund expanded substantially. They do not, by themselves, explain why. Inflation protection, portfolio construction and other motives require evidence beyond a list of securities.

Nor does the gold increase prove that Bitcoin financed it. Establishing such a rotation would require information about cash movements and the wider portfolio. Here, the Bitcoin share count stayed level while the GLD count rose.

Dartmouth’s crypto exposure extends beyond Bitcoin

Dartmouth also reported 304,803 shares in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF and 178,148 shares in the Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF. Those share counts likewise match its June table. Their September values were approximately $4.9 million and $4.5 million respectively.

The fund names describe distinct underlying exposures. Combining their dollar values can show the size of the reported crypto-linked positions, but it does not turn them into one interchangeable investment. Bitcoin, Ether and Solana can respond differently to network developments, and a staking product introduces mechanics that a straightforward Bitcoin trust does not have.

NewsBTC’s recent report on JPMorgan’s crypto-linked securities holdings shows another reason to inspect the actual instrument before interpreting an institutional total.

The reporting clock is still September’s

The SEC’s Form 13F guidance explains the delayed quarterly reporting framework. These disclosures are a record of reportable securities holdings, not a complete picture of each university’s assets or a live trading feed.

That timing matters after November’s sustained Bitcoin ETF withdrawals. A September position can coexist with subsequent market selling, and the latest filings cannot show whether either university changed its exposure after quarter-end.

The evidence is specific but useful: both reported stable Bitcoin ETF share counts through September, while Harvard’s gold holding expanded sharply. The next comparable filing will show whether that pattern survived the market’s later reversal.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: 7 Major Banks Reveal XRP ETF Holdings in Latest SEC Filings
summary: JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley were among seven banks reporting XRP-linked ETF holdings in their latest SEC filings. The disclosures spanned U.S., Canadian, and European institutions using spot funds, futures products, and other strategies. Global Banks Report XRP ETF Holdings J...
content:
JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley were among seven banks reporting XRP-linked ETF holdings in their latest SEC filings. The disclosures spanned U.S., Canadian, and European institutions using spot funds, futures products, and other strategies.

Key Takeaways

  • JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley disclosed XRP fund stakes.
  • Intesa’s $27.2 million position led the seven banks examined.
  • Holdings spanned spot, futures, leveraged, and options-based strategies.

Global Banks Report XRP ETF Holdings

JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley were among seven banks that disclosed XRP-linked ETF holdings in SEC filings submitted Nov. 9-16. UBS, Intesa Sanpaolo, National Bank of Canada, and Bank of Montreal completed the group, whose Sept. 30 positions totaled approximately $29.4 million. Nov. 16 was the SEC’s third-quarter Form 13F deadline.

Most of that value came from Italian banking group Intesa Sanpaolo, which had 989.2 billion euros in total assets as of Sept. 30. Its latest securities filing detailed $27.21 million across two funds. Its 712,319 Grayscale XRP Trust ETF shares were worth $20.52 million, while 402,750 Bitwise XRP ETF shares carried a $6.70 million valuation. Both products come from crypto investment managers and hold XRP directly.

That total reflected two developments: a new Bitwise position and a higher valuation for Intesa’s existing Grayscale stake. The Grayscale share count matched its earlier quarterly disclosure, when the position was worth $14.42 million.

These disclosures cover investments managed for clients or firms’ own accounts through Form 13F, a quarterly report required of institutional managers overseeing at least $100 million in qualifying securities. The positions represent ownership of fund shares, with the underlying assets or contracts held within the funds.

Banks Took Different Routes Into XRP Funds

The mix of products extended beyond funds holding XRP directly. Swiss bank and wealth manager UBS, with $1.66 trillion in total assets as of Sept. 30, disclosed $1.91 million in its quarterly holdings report filed Nov. 10, including approximately $1.59 million in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF. That fund tracks XRP through futures contracts.

UBS’s smaller positions added leverage and income strategies to the mix. Teucrium 2x Long Daily XRP and ProShares Ultra XRP seek twice XRP’s daily performance before fees and expenses, while Amplify’s XRP 3% Monthly Option Income ETF uses options to generate income. Other entries included another leveraged fund and a strategy combining S&P 500 exposure with XRP.

The futures-based route also appeared at Bank of America, which had $3.43 trillion in total assets as of Sept. 30. Its quarterly securities filing, submitted Nov. 16, listed 13,260 Volatility Shares XRP ETF shares worth $106,610. Both banks therefore used the same futures-based vehicle, despite their different position sizes.

Morgan Stanley, which had $1.69 trillion in total assets as of Sept. 30, used a different combination, reporting $116,097 across Franklin, REX-Osprey, and Bitwise in its quarterly XRP fund holdings filed Nov. 13. Franklin accounted for $111,885, while REX-Osprey, which offers spot XRP exposure, represented $3,098. Bitwise made up the remaining $1,114.

The same Bitwise fund connected those disclosures with JPMorgan Chase’s holdings. The bank had $5.1 trillion in total assets as of Sept. 30. Its Bitwise XRP ETF disclosure, filed Nov. 12, showed 539 shares worth $8,996.

Canadian Banks and Nonbank Investors Also Held XRP Funds

Among Canadian commercial lenders, National Bank of Canada disclosed 330 Bitwise XRP ETF shares worth $5,485 in its quarterly holdings report filed Nov. 16. The bank had 635 billion Canadian dollars in total assets as of July 31. Its position added a Canadian lender to the institutions using the same fund as Intesa, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan.

Bank of Montreal, which had 1.5 trillion Canadian dollars in total assets as of July 31, also used XRP-linked funds, combining two distinct products. Its quarterly securities report, filed Nov. 9, showed $4,267 split between $3,924 in REX-Osprey and $343 in ProShares Ultra XRP. That combination paired spot exposure with a leveraged strategy.

Outside banking, trading firm Jane Street, which provides buy and sell quotes, reported $23.50 million in XRP-linked fund shares on Nov. 12. Its largest positions included Bitwise, Franklin, and Canary at approximately $12.20 million, $5.00 million, and $3.13 million, respectively. The total excluded separately reported put and call options.

Filings also showed exposure at Rakuten, a Japanese group operating online shopping, banking, and mobile services. Its Bitwise XRP ETF position comprised 6,690 shares worth $111,255 as of Sept. 30.

Those September holdings preceded a weaker stretch for fund flows. U.S. spot XRP ETFs recorded $19.13 million in net withdrawals from Nov. 9 to 13, with Grayscale and Bitwise accounting for the largest outflows.

title: Hong Kong Reaffirms Year-End Crypto Licensing Bill as Tokenized Funds Expand
summary: Paul Chan’s November 16 speech reiterates a year-end licensing bill and puts expanding tokenized funds into a wider accountability framework.
content:
TL;DR

  • Paul Chan reiterated the year-end bill timetable on November 16.
  • The proposed perimeter would include dealing, advice, management and custody.
  • Tokenized products and continuous trading create distinct oversight needs.

Hong Kong’s Financial Secretary Paul Chan has reaffirmed plans to introduce a bill before the end of 2026 expanding the city’s digital-asset licensing framework. Speaking on November 16, he linked that regulatory work with a market moving toward regular use of tokenized investment products. The message was that more activity on blockchains still needs identifiable institutions responsible for the services around it.

Licensing would follow the service being provided

Chan’s Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum speech names dealing, advice, management and custody as activities to be brought within the perimeter. He also highlighted the two licensed stablecoin issuers and the emergence of around-the-clock trading in tokenized money-market funds.

The timetable is a reiteration, not a newly enacted rule. In a November 4 Legislative Council reply, the government said it planned to amend the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance and extend the existing trading-platform regime. That earlier explanation helps locate the proposal: the focus is the businesses handling digital assets and the functions they perform.

For a customer, the same investment can involve several such functions. One company might recommend it, another execute the purchase and another safeguard the resulting holding. A useful regulatory structure has to make responsibility visible at each handoff.

The fund market gives the proposal a practical setting

The November 4 government reply reported 17 authorised retail investment products with tokenized classes at the end of September, representing about HK$10.3 billion in those classes. These included money-market funds and gold-related products. The figure concerns a defined set of investment products; it should not be presented as the size of Hong Kong’s entire digital-asset market.

The Securities and Futures Commission’s October 26 approval allowed secondary trading of ChinaAMC’s Hong Kong-dollar and US-dollar digital money-market funds on a licensed virtual-asset platform. Secondary trading lets investors exchange existing interests rather than relying solely on subscriptions and redemptions with a fund.

That creates a different set of questions from simply recording ownership on a blockchain. Investors need meaningful prices, sufficient counterparties and a clear understanding of how traded units relate to their rights in the underlying product.

Continuous trading changes the operating burden

If a platform offers trading through a weekend, its customer support, security and controls have to account for that window. Yet the assets held by a fund may trade on a different schedule. A round-the-clock token does not ensure that its underlying market has become equally liquid at every hour.

The cash side is another dependency. Hong Kong’s EnsembleTX settlement work addresses how tokenized money and investment transactions can fit together. The trading venue, fund, custodian and payment service each need a consistent view of what has completed and what remains outstanding.

Stablecoin distribution raises similar questions about access and redemption. Anchorpoint’s planned native HKDAP expansion shows why a network integration and the conditions under which customers can use a product are separate milestones. A new route for transferring an asset does not by itself explain every holder’s rights.

The bill will determine the next set of boundaries

Chan’s speech does not itself set final licence conditions or establish a commencement date for the expanded regime. Those details matter to firms deciding whether to add a service, change a custody arrangement or work through another authorised provider.

The most useful next evidence will be the legislative text and its treatment of different business models. Clear definitions can help firms determine where their obligations begin, while practical transition arrangements affect how existing customers are served.

Hong Kong’s challenge is now partly one of coordination: allowing more products and trading hours while keeping responsibility legible. A tokenized market will be easier to evaluate when investors can identify who owes them what, who controls a transaction and which regulator oversees each service.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Nvidia shares fall 4% as board reportedly rules out Huang return
summary: The chipmaker’s board is reportedly focused on investigating Huang’s conduct, even as a petition calling for his reinstatement gathers more than 187,000 signatures.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 16, 2026

The chipmaker’s board is reportedly focused on investigating Huang’s conduct, even as a petition calling for his reinstatement gathers more than 187,000 signatures.

Nvidia’s board is reportedly not considering reinstating co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, despite a growing campaign for his return and public support from US President Donald Trump, as the chipmaker’s shares fell 4.1% on Monday.

The decline came as Bitcoin and US equities faced pressure ahead of Nvidia’s quarterly earnings and following Anthropic’s IPO announcement, adding to nerves around the artificial intelligence sector.

A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that Nvidia’s board was not discussing Huang’s return and remained focused on investigating his conduct. ABC News separately confirmed with a source familiar with the matter that the board was not considering reinstating him as CEO.

Huang resigned last week following reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with an alleged Chinese spy, with chief financial officer Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO. Nvidia’s shares have fallen 27% from a month ago.

The report comes despite growing support for his return. A public petition set up last week called “Stand with Jensen” has attracted more than 187,000 signatures, according to its organizers, who list Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney among its supporters.

US President Donald Trump also weighed in, saying Monday he would not mind seeing Jensen Huang return ‌as chief executive officer of Nvidia.

“I would certainly not mind seeing that,” he told reporters as he departed the White House for a trip to China. “He could return. There’s a big group of people that would like him to return.”
