title: Bitcoin Price Holiday Forecast: Claude and ChatGPT See Red, Grok Goes Green
summary: With bitcoin’s price trading between $63,500 to $65,280 per unit after plunging to a recent low of $61,947, uncertainty continues to grip the cryptocurrency market. As 2026 approaches its conclusion, Bitcoin.com News is putting artificial intelligence to the test, asking a collection of leading AI c...
content:
With bitcoin’s price trading between $63,500 to $65,280 per unit after plunging to a recent low of $61,947, uncertainty continues to grip the cryptocurrency market. As 2026 approaches its conclusion, Bitcoin.com News is putting artificial intelligence to the test, asking a collection of leading AI chatbots to forecast bitcoin’s price on Dec. 31 and explain whether further losses or recovery lie ahead.

Key Takeaways

  • Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok read the same bitcoin backdrop but found different clues about what comes next.
  • The forecasts reveal an unexpected point of agreement beneath the competing year-end targets.
  • One looming December event could put the models’ assumptions to the test.

Data for this predictive analysis, drawing on five distinct AI models, was collected on Nov. 15, 2026, at 9 p.m. Eastern time. Any links in responses added by Bitcoin.com News editors.

Bitcoin’s Year-End AI Forecasts Are In—and the Bulls Barely Showed Up

Bitcoin’s price downturn has left investors confronting an increasingly complicated year-end outlook, with institutional withdrawals, persistent selling pressure, and uncertainty surrounding the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy weighing on sentiment. The cryptocurrency has recovered modestly from its recent low, but whether that rebound represents the beginning of a meaningful recovery or another temporary interruption in a broader decline remains an open question.

With only 45 days remaining in 2026, the market faces a narrowing window to reverse its recent losses. Against this backdrop, Bitcoin.com News conducted an experiment involving several prominent artificial intelligence (AI) models, presenting each with identical market conditions and asking for a specific bitcoin price prediction for Dec. 31, 2026.

Rather than soliciting vague bullish or bearish commentary from the five models, the exercise demands a precise numerical forecast, supporting rationale, and an assessment of potential downside and upside scenarios. The objective is to examine where the models agree, where their expectations diverge, and how convincingly they interpret one of bitcoin’s most unsettled periods of the year.

The test conducted on Nov. 15, 2026, included Claude Fable 5.2 Medium Intelligence, ChatGPT Astra High Intelligence, Grok Expert, Gemini Argon, and Qwen 3.7 Plus. The prompt given to each model was as follows:

Today is Nov. 15, 2026. Bitcoin (BTC) trades at $65,280 after recently falling to $61,947. For a Bitcoin.com News experiment, forecast bitcoin’s exact price on Dec. 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Consider market trends, ETF flows, institutional demand, Federal Reserve policy, liquidity, sentiment and historical cycles.

Provide: One exact year-end price prediction with a brief explanation of the three main factors. Specific bearish and bullish price targets. A confidence percentage with an associated price range. Whether bitcoin will finish above or below $65,280 and the biggest risk to your forecast. Use only information available by Nov. 16, 2026. Avoid invented statistics. Make your best prediction despite uncertainty. Conclude in this exact format:

Dec. 31, 2026, BTC price prediction: $XX,XXX

Bearish scenario: $XX,XXX

Bullish scenario: $XX,XXX

Confidence: XX% (price range)

Year-end direction: Higher or lower than $65,280

CLAUDE FABLE 5.2 MEDIUM INTELLIGENCE ANSWER:

Prediction: $61,800 on Dec. 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Reasoning

Bitcoin is in a liquidation-driven downtrend against a hostile macro backdrop, so my base case is a small further loss, not a rebound. Three factors drive that.

First, Fed policy. The Fed made its first hike in more than three years in September and paused in October, and futures now unanimously expect a December hike, with half-point odds at 15%. Tighter liquidity lands three weeks before the target date.

Second, ETF flows. Spot bitcoin ETFs shed about $1.91 billion over seven straight sessions from Nov. 5 to Nov. 13, per Farside. Until that streak breaks, the marginal institutional buyer is a seller.

Third, technical damage and cycle position. BTC fell about 23% from its Nov. 4 high to $62,081 and broke below its 200-week moving average near $67,992, which is now resistance. 2026 is also the post-peak year of the four-year cycle, historically a weak one.

Offsetting this, roughly $750 million in liquidations, nearly 80% of them longs, has flushed leverage. I expect a relief bounce toward $68,000 that fails, then a year-end drift to the $62,000 support, helped by tax-loss selling.

Scenarios

Bearish, $52,000: The Fed hikes 50 basis points or signals a January follow-up, ETF redemptions continue, and $60,000 breaks.

Bullish, $74,000: The Fed delivers a 25-point hike with softer guidance, ETF flows turn positive, and BTC reclaims the 200-week average and the $70,000 level.

Probability: 50% that BTC closes between $54,000 and $70,000. This is my own estimate, based on bitcoin’s typical six-week volatility.

Direction: Below $65,280.

Key invalidator: The Dec. 9 FOMC decision. A hold, or a hike paired with a clear signal that tightening is finished, would likely trigger short covering and renewed ETF inflows and push BTC well above my target.

Verified vs. assumed

Verified from Nov. 10 to 15 reporting: The price low, ETF outflow total, liquidation figures, 200-week average level, Fed rate path and hike odds.

Assumptions: The failed bounce, tax-loss selling pressure, the cycle analogy holding, and all probabilities and price targets.

Not independently verified: Your $65,280 quote, though it matches reports of a Sunday recovery above $65,000.

Dec. 31, 2026, BTC price prediction: $61,800

Bearish scenario: $52,000

Bullish scenario: $74,000

Confidence: 50% ($54,000 to $70,000)

Year-end direction: Lower than $65,280

CHATGPT ASTRA HIGH INTELLIGENCE ANSWER:

My base-case forecast is $62,000 at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 31, 2026, approximately 5% below $65,280. Using your starting price and evidence published before the Nov. 16 cutoff, I expect stabilization after further volatility, with three factors driving the forecast:

ETF selling outweighs corporate buying. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost approximately $2.35 billion across Nov. 2–13, according to Farside’s daily figures. Institutional demand has not disappeared: Strategy disclosed an $81.9 million bitcoin purchase during Nov. 2–8. My judgment is that continued buying cushions declines but cannot sustain a recovery unless ETF withdrawals ease.

Fed policy threatens liquidity. The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% in October, and Governor Christopher Waller subsequently raised the possibility of a half-point December increase. Higher financing costs and attractive cash yields would restrain speculative demand. My base case assumes continued monetary restraint rather than a year-end liquidity boost.

The downtrend outweighs rebound potential. Your $61,947 low and subsequent bounce leave bitcoin below the $73,000–$75,000 recovery zone identified by Coinbase’s Nov. 13 analysis. Fear can fuel sharp rebounds, while historical four-year cycles suggest a possible bottoming period. Neither establishes that a durable recovery will arrive within six weeks.

The $48,000 bearish scenario assumes renewed forced selling and persistent withdrawals; the $82,000 bullish scenario assumes sustained ETF inflows and easing rate concerns. The biggest risk to my lower-price forecast is a sudden reversal in institutional flows that drives a stronger recovery than expected.

Confidence is subjective: I assign a 65% probability to the stated range, not to hitting the exact price; this is not a statistically calibrated interval.

Dec. 31, 2026, BTC price prediction: $62,000

Bearish scenario: $48,000

Bullish scenario: $82,000

Confidence: 65% ($50,000–$78,000)

Year-end direction: Lower than $65,280

GROK EXPERT ANSWER:

Dec. 31, 2026, BTC price prediction: $68,420

Bitcoin is trading near $65,280 after a drop to roughly $61,947–$62,080, down about 48% from its October 2025 all-time high near $126,000 and roughly 25% year-to-date from early-2026 levels around $87,000–$88,000. With about six weeks left, the setup points to a modest year-end recovery rather than a sharp reversal or further deep decline.

Three main factors drive this view:

  1. Extreme fear and oversold conditions. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index has fallen to 10 (extreme fear), with heavy long liquidations (roughly $1–2 billion in recent sessions) and RSI readings in oversold territory. Historically, such extremes have often preceded technical bounces even in corrective phases.
  2. ETF flows and institutional demand. US spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $2.35 billion in net outflows over the two weeks ending November 13, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for the large majority. Cumulative inflows remain strongly positive long-term (around $54–55 billion), but recent redemptions signal caution and have removed a key source of buying. Stabilization or modest year-end rebalancing could support prices without requiring a full trend change.
  3. Federal Reserve policy and liquidity. The Fed holds the funds rate at 3.75–4.00% after its October meeting, and markets price a high probability (roughly 89–92%) of a 25 basis-point hike at the December 9 meeting amid sticky inflation data (core CPI around 0.3%). Higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like bitcoin and keep broader liquidity tighter, limiting upside even if the hike is largely priced in. Cycle context adds nuance: the post-April 2024 halving peak arrived in October 2025, and the current ~48–52% drawdown is shallower than prior bears (typically 77–85%). Some analysts (including Standard Chartered) still see potential for a cycle low near recent levels and higher year-end targets, though those appear optimistic given current momentum.

Bearish scenario: $57,500

A break of recent lows toward or below the June 2026 area, driven by a larger-than-expected Fed hike, continued heavy ETF outflows, and further deleveraging.

Bullish scenario: $79,200

A reclaim of nearby moving averages (around the 50- or 200-day) if ETF flows stabilize or reverse and risk sentiment improves after the December Fed decision.

Confidence: 42% (price range $61,000–$74,000)

The base case sits in the middle of a wide distribution reflecting high uncertainty. Algorithmic and technical models cluster in broad $52,000–$73,000 bands for year-end, with limited consensus above current levels in the near term.

Year-end direction: Higher than $65,280

Biggest risk to the forecast: An acceleration of ETF outflows combined with a more hawkish Fed outcome (or hotter data that raises odds of a larger hike), which could override oversold technicals and push prices toward or below recent lows before year-end.

GEMINI ARGON ANSWER:

Bitcoin is projected to finish the year at $62,450 on Dec. 31, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET, trending lower than its Nov. 15 price of $65,280.

Three Main Factors Driving the Forecast

Restrictive Federal Reserve Policy and Inflation Pressures: Following the Federal Reserve’s decision on Sept. 16, 2026, to raise the top of its target interest rate range to 4.00% (3.75%–4.00%), macroeconomic headwinds have intensified. With annual Producer Price Index (PPI) inflation still elevated at 6.5% in October, fed funds futures price in an 89% probability of another 25-basis-point rate hike at the upcoming Dec. 9 FOMC meeting. Higher yields and a stronger U.S. dollar continue to drain speculative liquidity from risk assets.

Sustained Spot ETF Outflows and Liquidity Contraction: Institutional demand through U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs has reversed sharply, erasing 2026’s earlier net inflows. Spot ETFs recorded roughly $1.07 billion in net outflows over five trading days—and $1.91 billion over a seven-day stretch in mid-November—bringing 30-day estimated institutional demand down to -284,000 BTC. Concurrently, broader crypto market liquidity has tightened following an $11.5 billion drop in stablecoin supply and $1.64 billion in leveraged long liquidations when bitcoin broke below $70,000 on Nov. 13.

Post-Halving Cycle Exhaustion and Technical Breakdown: In alignment with historical four-year cycle patterns, bitcoin peaked at an all-time high of $126,080 in October 2025 (roughly 18 months after the 2024 halving) and has entered a multi-quarter cyclical drawdown, sitting nearly 49% below its peak. Technically, bitcoin is trading below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages after trending downward from its Sept. 21 high of $86,597, encouraging year-end institutional tax-loss harvesting and defensive positioning.

Scenario Targets, Confidence & Key Risk

Bearish Scenario ($55,200): If the Federal Reserve executes a 25-basis-point hike on Dec. 9 alongside hawkish 2027 guidance while spot ETF outflows accelerate into year-end tax-loss selling, bitcoin is likely to break below psychological support at $60,000 and its 12-month low of $58,566 (set around June 30–July 1, 2026), sliding toward the mid-$50,000 range.

Bullish Scenario ($72,800): If the Federal Reserve surprises markets by pausing rate hikes on Dec. 9 and spot ETF flows stabilize, short-covering and year-end portfolio rebalancing could push bitcoin back above the $68,400–$70,000 resistance zone toward the upper bound of near-term consensus estimates ($65,000–$73,000).

Confidence & Price Range: There is a 65% confidence probability that bitcoin will close the year within the $58,500 to $68,500 range, bounded by its 12-month cyclical support at $58,566 and heavy technical resistance below $70,000.

Biggest Risk to the Forecast: The primary risk to this mildly bearish forecast is an unexpected dovish pivot or pause by the Federal Reserve on Dec. 9 paired with a sudden resurgence in spot ETF inflows. Because market sentiment is heavily skewed toward a rate hike (89% odds) and derivatives positioning has turned defensive after recent liquidations, any relief in Treasury yields or U.S. dollar strength could trigger an aggressive short squeeze back above $70,000 before Dec. 31.

Dec. 31, 2026, BTC price prediction: $62,450

Bearish scenario: $55,200

Bullish scenario: $72,800

Confidence: 65% ($58,500 – $68,500)

Year-end direction: Lower than $65,280

QWEN 3.7 PLUS ANSWER:

Based on market data and trends available through mid-November 2026, here is the comprehensive year-end forecast for bitcoin.

Exact Year-End Price Prediction: $68,450

Three Main Factors:

  1. Federal Reserve Policy & Liquidity: Global liquidity remains the primary macroeconomic driver for risk assets. Market expectations around the Fed’s interest rate trajectory will dictate year-end momentum; steady rates or dovish signals would support a modest rally, while hawkish surprises would cap upside potential.
  2. ETF Flows & Institutional Demand: Spot bitcoin ETF flows have been volatile, recently contributing to price dips below key technical levels like the 200-day moving average. However, persistent long-term institutional accumulation continues to establish a robust support floor in the low-$60,000s, preventing deeper market capitulation.
  3. Historical Cycles & Sentiment: Historical post-halving patterns indicate that late in the cycle year, bitcoin often enters a consolidation phase rather than experiencing a parabolic advance or a severe crash. Current market sentiment is cautious but stable, favoring a range-bound finish to the year as traders position for 2027.

Bearish Scenario: $58,500

If ETF outflows accelerate and macroeconomic data forces the Fed to maintain restrictive rates, bitcoin could break below the recent $61,947 low and test deeper support zones near the mid-2026 intraday lows.

Bullish Scenario: $74,200

A surprise dovish pivot from the Fed or a sudden surge in institutional demand could propel BTC through the $70,000 resistance level, targeting the upper bound of its recent trading range before hitting the established $80,000 macroeconomic cap.

Confidence: 65% (Price range: $63,000 – $72,000)

Year-End Direction: Higher than $65,280

Biggest Risk to Forecast: A sudden, severe macroeconomic shock (such as an unexpected inflation spike forcing aggressive monetary tightening) or a systemic regulatory event that triggers sustained, heavy spot ETF outflows, which would break the critical $60,000 institutional support floor.

Dec. 31, 2026, BTC price prediction: $68,450

Bearish scenario: $58,500

Bullish scenario: $74,200

Confidence: 65% ($63,000 – $72,000)

Year-end direction: Higher than $65,280

Striking Consensus or Dangerous Groupthink

Altogether, five AI models provided responses within a relatively tight range. The real insight is their methodological uniformity: All invoke the same trio of ETF outflows, Fed hawkishness, and technical breakdown. That sameness suggests either striking consensus or dangerous groupthink. Grok and Qwen alone anticipate upside, a contrarian position potentially more valuable than the majority’s caution.

Most telling is the AIs’ shared assumption that the recent cascade of selling reflects rational repricing rather than capitulation. If that premise fails, then their precise year-end targets amount to elaborate justifications for a passing panic. The market’s actual course will likely make a mockery of those confidence intervals, as six-week crypto forecasts have historically invited it to do.

title: Backpack Wins US Clearing Registration as Separate Exchange Bid Remains Pending
summary: Backpack Clearing’s CFTC registration covers specified derivatives, while TLD Markets’ separate US exchange application remains pending.
content:
TL;DR

  • The CFTC registered TLD Clearing, doing business as Backpack Clearing, on November 13.
  • Its scope includes margined futures and specified fully collateralized derivatives.
  • TLD Markets’ separate exchange application remains listed as pending.

Backpack has secured a US derivatives-clearing registration, adding a regulated institution for handling the obligations behind trades. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission registered TLD Clearing, doing business as Backpack Clearing, on November 13. The approval is a meaningful part of the group’s market-infrastructure plans, while a separate application to operate an exchange remains pending.

Clearing approval covers a defined function

The CFTC’s public register permits Backpack Clearing to clear margined futures, along with fully collateralized futures, options on futures and swaps. This identifies the clearinghouse’s authorised scope; it does not show that every potential contract has launched.

A clearinghouse becomes the central counterparty to accepted trades and manages the resulting obligations. Its job differs from matching buyers and sellers on an exchange. A trading screen can display an executed order quickly, but the market also needs arrangements for collecting collateral, settling gains and losses and dealing with a participant that cannot pay.

The distinction is relevant to the broader industry push toward integrated derivatives operations. Coinbase’s earlier clearing registration showed another crypto group building this part of its infrastructure, under its own approved scope.

The application describes how risk would be handled

Backpack’s clearing-activities submission describes an intended central-counterparty model for contracts listed on registered markets. It includes initial and variation margin, risk-based requirements and default-management procedures. The filing also describes legally separate exchange, clearing and brokerage entities working within a coordinated framework.

That separation matters when a group offers several services under one familiar brand. A customer needs to know which entity holds its account, which one accepts a trade for clearing and which rules apply if something goes wrong. Shared ownership does not make those roles interchangeable.

The application contemplated a phased product rollout. Its list of possible future products should therefore be read as a plan subject to the relevant approvals and operating capacity, rather than a current trading menu. Clearing registration alone does not establish availability, customer eligibility or the amount of market liquidity.

The order creates continuing responsibilities

The registration order records commitments to enforce clearing-member standards and maintain member funds separately from the clearinghouse’s own funds. It also says changes to material facts or circumstances may require a new or amended order.

These are operating obligations that continue after the approval date. For a clearing business, reliable performance depends on how it handles changing exposures and exceptional events, not only on passing an initial regulatory assessment.

Imagine a sharp market move that leaves one member owing more collateral. The clearinghouse needs timely prices, dependable calls for funds and a credible process if that member fails. The practical strength of the model would become visible through those controls and its ability to complete settlements under stress.

The exchange decision is still a separate step

The CFTC’s record for TLD Markets lists its designated-contract-market application as pending, dated April 22, 2026. That is the status shown in the public record reviewed for this report. The clearing decision should not be described as approval of that separate exchange application.

Nor should the US registration be blended with other Backpack-branded activity, such as tokenized-equity collateral used in Kamino’s Solana lending market. Different products can sit within different legal entities and regulatory arrangements even when their branding overlaps.

For Backpack, the immediate achievement is a registered clearing operation with an identified scope. The next commercial milestones are the remaining relevant permissions and clearly documented products, participants and launch arrangements. Those details will determine what traders can actually access through the US structure.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Custodia Bank loses Supreme Court bid for direct Fed payment access
summary: The Supreme Court refused to hear Custodia Bank’s appeal, meaning a lower court ruling allowing the Fed to reject account applications will stand.
content:
The United States Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear an appeal from crypto-focused bank Custodia, effectively ending the bank’s latest legal effort to gain direct access to the Federal Reserve’s payment system.

Custodia is a Wyoming-chartered bank founded by Caitlin Long. The bank has been trying for a Fed master account since 2020, which would allow it to process payments directly without relying on third-party financial institutions.

Now, the Supreme Court’s Monday decision means an earlier ruling allowing the Fed to reject applications from eligible banks will remain in effect.

The case highlights some of the challenges crypto-facing banks face in gaining direct access to the US payment system. Still, even if state-chartered banks qualify for master accounts, the Fed does not have to approve every application.

In a dissent issued in March, US Circuit Judge Timothy Tymkovich criticized the appeals court’s decision to give Federal Reserve banks discretion over master accounts.

“Without a master account, a bank cannot operate in the modern banking system,” Tymkovich wrote, arguing that the ruling effectively gives the Fed the power to override state banking decisions.

A timeline of events

Custodia first sued the Federal Reserve in 2022 after waiting around two years for a decision on its master account application. The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City ended up rejecting the request in January 2023, citing concerns about risks linked to the bank’s crypto-focused business model.

In October 2025, a federal appeals court ruled against Custodia, finding that Federal Reserve banks did not have to grant master accounts to every eligible institution.

Related: Crypto among sectors ‘debanked’ by 9 major banks: US regulator

Cointelegraph previously reported that the court declined to reconsider its decision in March. This led Custodia to take its case to the Supreme Court.

The bank’s appeal also received support from the Blockchain Association, which argued that the Fed’s ability to reject applications could weaken the authority of state banking regulators.

Senator Cynthia Lummis and former Senator Patrick Toomey also filed a brief with the Supreme Court in August, supporting Custodia’s appeal.

Today’s decision comes as other crypto-focused banks seek access to the Fed’s payment system. In March, Kraken Financial received approval for a restricted account from the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City — the same regional bank that rejected Custodia’s application.

Notably, Kraken’s account was approved for an initial one-year period and allows it to send and receive payments through the Fed’s Fedwire system. However, the account has restrictions and does not offer all the services of a full master account.

Looking ahead, Custodia may still be able to apply for another master account or seek limited access to the Fed’s payment system under a separate proposal.

title: Justin Sun Prize Recognizes New Work on Two Erdős Problems, Highlighting AI’s Role in Mathematics
summary: Geneva, Switzerland, November 16, 2026 — The Office of Justin Sun today announced the latest recipients of the Justin Sun Prize, honoring work on Erdős problems —mathematical questions posed or popularized by Hungarian mathematician Paul Erdős that are often simple to state but difficult to solve. L...
content:
Geneva, Switzerland, November 16, 2026 — The Office of Justin Sun today announced the latest recipients of the Justin Sun Prize, honoring work on Erdős problems —mathematical questions posed or popularized by Hungarian mathematician Paul Erdős that are often simple to state but difficult to solve.

Liam Kruer, Jensen Kohlmeyer, and Liam Price are recognized for their work on JSP-000110 (Erdős Problem #97), and Peilin Liu (刘沛霖) is honored for a Lean formalization of JSP-000697 (Erdős Problem #841).

Kruer is an engineering student at Purdue University interested in the connections between mathematics, software, and design. Kohlmeyer is a mechanical engineering and mathematics student at Purdue. Price is an independent researcher. Liu holds a bachelor’s degree in mathematics from Shandong University and is pursuing a master’s degree in mathematics at the same university.

Erdős Problem #97 asks whether every convex polygon has a vertex from which no distance to the other vertices repeats too often. Kruer, Kohlmeyer, and Price worked on the problem by constructing a convex polygon in which every vertex has at least four other vertices exactly one unit away, and their work also addresses a broader version of the question. The three contributed equally to the mathematical solution and Lean formalization.

Erdős Problem #841 asks for how short a following interval can be while still supplying larger integers whose product with a given integer is a square. Liu contributed by producing a Lean formalization for the problem.

Kruer, Kohlmeyer, and Price disclosed substantial AI assistance and retained responsibility for the work, while Liu developed the formalization with help from Codex and ChatGPT Pro.

The announcement follows the prize’s recently launched pilot with MathDB, the mathematical research platform developed by Caltech Professor Tony Yue Yu and his team. The pilot introduced a formal submission and review process for AI-assisted research across 50 problems.

Details of each recipient’s contribution, including Lean source code and verification records, are available in the prize’s public GitHub repository. The prizes will be paid out in either USDT on TRON (TRC-20) or USDC on Ethereum (ERC-20), as each recipient chooses, subject to the applicable prize terms and compliance verification. For more information, please visit www.hejustinsun.com/prize.

About the Office of Justin Sun

The Office of Justin Sun supports Justin Sun’s global business, philanthropic and public initiatives across technology, blockchain, artificial intelligence, scientific research, investment, art and space exploration.

Justin Sun is the Ambassador and former Permanent Representative of Grenada to the World Trade Organization and the Founder of TRON. TRON is the leading blockchain for the stablecoin revolution, processing over $13 trillion in volume since its inception. In the world’s emerging markets, people rely on USDT on TRON to access the global financial system.

A protégé of Alibaba founder Jack Ma, Sun has been recognized internationally for his work in the digital asset industry, including a Forbes cover profile in April 2025 and multiple appearances on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list. In August 2025, he flew aboard Blue Origin’s NS-34 mission, becoming the 712th person in history to travel to space. His broader interests span technology, investment, philanthropy, art, gaming, and space exploration.

About Justin Sun Prize

The Justin Sun Prize is an academic initiative established by Justin Sun to support advances in mathematics, formal verification, and AI-assisted scientific discovery. The prize is decentralized and built around the principle that mathematical work should be judged by the strength, rigor, and verifiability of the proof itself, not the prestige or reputation of those submitting it.

Justin Sun established the prize in his own name as a long-term commitment to return wealth created through mathematics and technology back to mathematics itself. Its legacy is intended to be defined by the body of work it recognizes and the laureates whose discoveries stand the test of time. The prize links clearly defined mathematical challenges to machine-verifiable proof. Its guiding principles are openness, public benefit and open-source access.

title: German lawmakers back crypto freezes outside criminal cases
summary: Customs authorities could hold “suspicious” assets for 30 days under the bill, with court oversight for extensions and disputed confiscation.
content:
Germany’s lower house of parliament has passed a bill that would let customs authorities temporarily freeze cryptocurrency and other high-value assets suspected of having unlawful origins without first opening a criminal investigation.

The Bundestag passed the customs reform bill on Friday as part of a wider effort to combat money laundering and organized crime. The proposed procedure would target assets worth more than 100,000 euros and explicitly mentions cryptocurrencies.

Under the bill’s text approved by lawmakers, authorities would be able to hold assets for up to 30 days where there are factual indications of unlawful origins, according to a translated version. However, filing an application for confiscation could suspend those deadlines pending a court decision, and in contested cases, a court would have to be satisfied that the assets were of unlawful origin before ordering confiscation, effectively putting the burden of proof on the crypto holder.

German Social Democratic Party lawmaker Ingo Vogel said that the powers would allow authorities to pursue suspicious assets even when there are not yet grounds to open a criminal case, according to the Bundestag’s summary of the debate on the bill.

The bill still requires consent from the Bundesrat, Germany’s upper house of parliament, and is intended to take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.

Lawyers challenge asset seizure powers

Germany’s Federal Bar Association, known as BRAK, previously opposed the government’s draft in an Oct. 28 statement, warning that the meaning of unlawful origin is too vague and risks treating missing records as evidence of illicit wealth.

The association pointed to assets inherited through generations as one example where owners may lack a paper trail. It also questioned what the administrative process would add to Germany’s existing criminal confiscation rules.

German blockchain industry association Bundesblock also raised concerns about the treatment of digital assets in a March 31 submission on an earlier draft. It warned at the time that blockchain analysis should not automatically be treated as proof of ownership or control, and that incorrect wallet attribution could even infringe fundamental rights.

Related: Crypto adoption blooming in Germany, while UK is falling ‘behind,’ says CoinShares researcher

Movie2k judge proposes Bitcoin deal

Germany has already carried out large crypto seizures under existing law. As Cointelegraph reported, Saxony authorities sold 49,858 Bitcoin (BTC) linked to the Movie2k piracy investigation in 2024, raising about 2.6 billion euros, or $2.8 billion. At the time, prosecutors said the proceeds remained secured pending a court ruling on confiscation.

In a recent development, local outlet MDR reported on Friday that a Leipzig judge proposed ending proceedings against the main defendant in exchange for 40,000 BTC and a payment of 38 million euros for the potential victims. The proposal remains under consideration.

title: Binance hack may push institutions to outside custody, FalconX exec says
summary: FalconX’s Joshua Lim says the Binance hack could push institutions to keep crypto off exchanges and change how large investors trade in 2027.
content:
A major shift in institutional crypto trading could be on the horizon following the recent Binance hack, as security concerns may lead to more large investors keeping their assets outside exchanges, according to a FalconX executive.

In an exclusive interview with Cointelegraph at the Digital Asset Forum in New York City on Nov. 13, Joshua Lim, global head of markets at FalconX, a digital asset brokerage for institutional investors, said the Oct. 29 hack could make institutions more cautious about trading crypto and change how they store their assets.

“It’s actually quite bearish for more institutional participation in crypto,” Lim told Cointelegraph. He said traders initially played down the hack but later began to recognize its potential long-term impact.

As a result, Lim expects more institutions to turn to outside custody providers and trading firms that allow them to trade without keeping their crypto on exchanges, a shift he believes could become one of the biggest trends in 2027.

Binance hack could drive shift toward outside custody

North Korean-linked hackers stole about $6.4 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, making it the largest crypto theft on record, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis.

The shift toward keeping crypto outside exchanges already appeared to be underway even before the hack. In an October proposal, the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said industry practices were developing that reduced the need to move investment advisers’ client assets and regulated funds’ crypto holdings out of permitted custody for trading.

Lim pointed to Copper, a crypto custody provider, as one company that could benefit. Its ClearLoop service lets investors trade on supported exchanges while keeping their crypto with a separate company.

Copper said collateral protected by its ClearLoop service supported more than $240 billion in perpetual futures trading volume during the first quarter of 2026, more than double the amount a year earlier.

Lim explained that investors can keep their assets outside an exchange while receiving credited balances that allow them to trade on it. Under the brokerage model Lim described, a hedge fund can place trades through FalconX, which executes them using its own exchange accounts and relationships. Still, investors face risks tied to the firms holding their assets and settling their trades.

“For many players, facing a regulated entity like ours is more palatable,” Lim added.

Related: Crypto hack losses equal 57 cents per $1 earned onchain: Ark’s Valente

Bitcoin withdrawals from Binance rise after hack

Binance recorded large Bitcoin outflows in mid-November, although it is not clear whether they were linked to the hack.

According to CryptoQuant data, Binance recorded net withdrawals of about 2,771 Bitcoin (BTC) on Friday, followed by 2,708 BTC on Saturday and 5,636 BTC on Sunday — totaling about 11,115 BTC leaving the exchange than entered over those three days.

The withdrawals came as the broader crypto market was falling, with Bitcoin trading around $65,000 at 9:41 pm UTC Monday, down about 20% over the past month, according to CoinGecko.

However, the data does not show who moved the Bitcoin or why. Investors could have transferred their funds to personal wallets, companies that store crypto on their behalf, or to other exchanges.

How institutional crypto trading could change in 2027

Beyond concerns about exchange security, Lim expects other changes in how large investors trade in 2027. He said institutions want more ways to trade assets such as oil, gold and stock market indexes through crypto platforms, including outside regular market hours.

“You can respond quickly to news events when they happen,” Lim said, citing one of the benefits of 24/7 trading.

That type of trading is already taking place on Hyperliquid, a decentralized trading platform that offers contracts tied to traditional assets. As of Monday, Hyperliquid’s markets for traditional assets and other contracts had about $4.3 billion in open interest and recorded $3.9 billion in trading volume over 24 hours, according to data from Perpys.

But while crypto platforms are giving investors more ways to trade, Lim said the financial services needed to support those trades have not kept up, particularly when it comes to borrowing money and managing risk.

For example, investors can now trade oil through traditional futures markets, investment funds and crypto platforms. But lenders may treat trades on each platform separately, even when those trades balance each other out.

“There’s not enough players that can give you leverage or margin financing against all of these things collectively,” Lim said. “The risk netting is not quite there yet.”

title: Bitcoin Fear Hits Extreme Levels as Analyst Sees Contrarian Signal
summary: Bitcoin sentiment gauges showed extreme fear on Monday, Nov. 16, as investors faced sustained fund withdrawals and pressure on leveraged trades. Analysts considered whether widespread pessimism could favor a rebound, while uneven buying and shrinking stablecoin supply complicated that outlook. Extre...
content:
Bitcoin sentiment gauges showed extreme fear on Monday, Nov. 16, as investors faced sustained fund withdrawals and pressure on leveraged trades. Analysts considered whether widespread pessimism could favor a rebound, while uneven buying and shrinking stablecoin supply complicated that outlook.

Key Takeaways

  • Extreme fear spread across crypto sentiment gauges as pessimism deepened.
  • U.S. spot bitcoin funds recorded roughly $1.9 billion in net outflows.
  • Selective buying contrasted with liquidation risks and declining liquidity.

Extreme Fear Prompts a Contrarian Assessment

Extreme fear dominated bitcoin sentiment as Cryptoquant contributor Darkfost identified a potential contrarian signal on X on Nov. 16, stating:

“Extreme fear has finally taken over the market.”

He added: “With a score of 10, the Fear and Greed Index shows that Extreme Fear is now dominating investor sentiment on bitcoin.” He put the Fear and Greed Index’s 30-day average at 28.2, approaching readings seen in February and June, when bitcoin had traded lower.

In bitcoin market analysis, a contrarian signal runs against prevailing sentiment, suggesting widespread pessimism could precede a rebound. Comparing daily readings with a 30-day moving average, which smooths daily swings, the analyst remarked:

“This gives us an interesting contrarian signal right now.”

The analyst also included a chart that tracked bitcoin’s price alongside the Fear and Greed Index and its 30-day average. The latest sentiment reading of 10 stood below the average of 28.2, showing that daily sentiment had deteriorated more sharply than the broader monthly trend.

Santiment separately recorded bearish sentiment across bitcoin, ether, and XRP on Nov. 10. Bullish comments numbered 82 per 100 bearish ones for bitcoin, 88 for ether, and 49 for XRP. The analytics firm likewise interpreted that pessimism as potentially favorable for a recovery.

Three Gauges Show Widespread Pessimism

Alternative.me’s Fear and Greed Index stood at 10 on Nov. 16, unchanged from Sunday, versus 29 last week and 55 last month. Its zero-to-100 scale measures sentiment, with lower scores reflecting greater fear. Inputs include volatility, or price fluctuations, and momentum, the strength and direction of price moves.

Coinglass showed a sentiment reading of 11, classified as extreme fear, alongside bitcoin’s price history. Extreme fear accounted for 416 days, or 13.05%, of its displayed historical sample, compared with 31.74% for fear and 4.67% for extreme greed.

As of this writing, Coinmarketcap’s separate gauge registered 13 after hitting 12 earlier Monday, down from 29 a week earlier and 50 a month earlier. Its yearly range was 5 on Feb. 5 to 82 on Aug. 26. Inputs include expected price swings, demand for put and call options, bitcoin’s value relative to stablecoin supplies, and search and engagement data.

Fund Withdrawals Complicate the Recovery Case

On Sunday, Nov. 15, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao cited possible pressures behind the crypto sell-off, including roughly $1.9 billion in U.S. spot bitcoin fund outflows over seven sessions through Nov. 13. His other explanations included security concerns, inflation, politics, and competition for capital from initial public offerings. Zhao emphasized uncertainty about causation.

Glassnode’s Nov. 11 analysis identified a concentration of vulnerable bullish trades between $59,500 and $62,600. This liquidation cluster marked prices where many leveraged trades could be forcibly closed, adding selling pressure.

Buying remained uneven in Glassnode’s assessment, with accumulation among wallets holding 100-1,000 BTC and 1,000-10,000 BTC, while smaller holders and the largest group reduced balances. By Nov. 14, the firm reported that stablecoin supply had contracted by $17 billion over a month.

Bitcoin recently traded near $65,000, down more than 13% over the last week though up from a recent low near $62,000 over the weekend.

title: Unocoin Estimates $200,000 Loss as Backup-Key Finding Explains Wallet Transfers
summary: Unocoin's latest disclosure puts estimated losses at $200,000, while BitGo explains how customer-controlled keys could move funds outside its platform.
content:
TL;DR

  • Unocoin estimates a $200,000 cryptocurrency loss and says it will cover it.
  • BitGo says the affected Ethereum transfers used two keys controlled by Unocoin.
  • Potential data exposure and the route by which backup keys were compromised remain under investigation.

Unocoin has revised its account of a security incident that disrupted the Indian exchange, putting estimated cryptocurrency losses at about $200,000. The more significant technical finding is how transactions could proceed after the exchange asked its wallet providers to freeze activity.

Unocoin’s November 14 update identifies compromised backup keys as part of the explanation. The incident illustrates a distinction that can be easy to miss: suspending access to a service and removing the ability to authorize a blockchain transaction are separate things.

The exchange has changed its loss assessment

Unocoin said three operational hot wallets were compromised and promised to fund the identified loss from its own resources. Its earlier assessment had not identified missing cryptocurrency. The company also disclosed possible exposure of customer information, while saying it had found no evidence that KYC documents were accessed.

Those findings remain subject to investigation. An initial loss estimate is useful for assessing scale, but it is not the same as a final reconciliation of every asset and transaction. Potential information exposure also needs to be assessed separately from the amount of cryptocurrency taken.

That distinction matters for customers. Replacing coins can restore an account balance; it cannot make exposed contact or account information private again. A financial remedy and a data-security response address different consequences.

Two customer-held keys could authorize transfers

BitGo’s November 13 account says the affected Ethereum wallet used a two-of-three multisignature arrangement. Unocoin controlled the user and backup keys, while BitGo controlled the third. BitGo says the reviewed transfers used the two Unocoin keys and were broadcast outside its platform.

The design permits an owner to recover assets without depending on the service provider. That is valuable when a provider is unavailable, but the same independence means that the provider’s refusal to sign cannot prevent two other valid keys from acting together.

BitGo’s wallet documentation distinguishes self-custody arrangements from its custody products, including differences in who controls keys. A provider’s name therefore does not, by itself, tell a reader who had final authority over a particular wallet.

Recovery controls deserve the same scrutiny

The broader control question is whether emergency credentials are separated effectively from everyday systems. A recovery mechanism has to remain available to its legitimate owner while being difficult for an intruder to assemble with other signing material.

NewsBTC’s coverage of business Bitcoin accounts with team approvals examined another part of that problem: permission to request or approve a transfer is not necessarily identical to possession of the cryptographic keys.

Combining several safeguards can help, but their independence matters. Two approvals provide less protection if one compromised system can obtain both. This is an architectural lesson from the reported signing arrangement, not a determination of the still-unknown route into Unocoin’s backup storage.

The next update needs to reconcile the whole incident

Unocoin says it is rebuilding infrastructure and investigating how the backup material was compromised. A convincing follow-up would connect that forensic explanation with a complete accounting of losses, restored services and the handling of potentially exposed information.

BitGo’s wider commercial growth, covered in NewsBTC’s report on its quarterly results, shows how large the custody and infrastructure business has become. Scale makes clear descriptions of individual service arrangements more valuable, particularly when several companies participate in one transaction process.

The available disclosures narrow the explanation considerably. They identify which keys authorized the reviewed Ethereum transfers. They do not yet provide a complete account of how those keys were obtained or establish that every part of the incident has been resolved.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Crypto Market Value Jumped 40% in Q3, but Retail Spot Trading Didn’t Follow
summary:
eToro's funded user accounts jumped 18% over the past year, yet its clients placed 62% fewer crypto trades this October than a year earlier. That disconnect captures the paradox of the third quarter: crypto prices staged 40% rebound, but the retail spot trading volumes did not. 
Across major central...
content:
2026-11-16T23:40:00.000+02:00

Monday, 16/11/2026 | 21:40 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Crypto market value rose 39.6% in Q3, while spot turnover on the largest exchanges fell 14.2%.
  • Bitcoin ETF inflows returned as Robinhood and Coinbase expanded their prediction-market businesses.

eToro's funded user accounts jumped 18% over the past year, yet its clients placed 62% fewer crypto trades this October than a year earlier. That disconnect captures the paradox of the third quarter: crypto prices staged 40% rebound, but the retail spot trading volumes did not.

Across major centralised platforms, spot trading turnover contracted by 14.2% sequentially in Q3, while direct crypto execution on mainstream consumer platforms remained in a deep slump compared to 2025.

Crypto trading volume on the Robinhood App fell 48%, while Coinbase’s consumer spot volume dropped 59%. Coinbase also reported 7.4 million monthly transacting users across its products, down from 9.3 million, mainly because fewer customers traded. At the same time, total crypto market capitalisation jumped by 39.6% over the same period.

Bitcoin ETF Inflows Returned as Spot Trading Stayed Weak

With trading revenues pressured on venues like Coinbase and Robinhood, retail capital has increasingly bypassed direct spot tokens entirely, diverting instead into spot ETFs, leveraged perpetuals, and booming prediction markets.

US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $6.34 billion of net inflows in Q3, according to SoSoValue data, after roughly $5 billion of outflows in the second quarter. As those purchases are trades in fund shares, they do not appear in a broker’s direct crypto trading figures.

Earlier in the year, institutions accounted for 72% of spot volume on Wintermute’s OTC desk, up from 59% a year earlier. The firm described a market “with retail largely absent and preoccupied with equities.”

Trading Platforms Expand Beyond Crypto Spot

Prediction market volume reached a record $188 billion in Q3, 21 times the level a year earlier, according to CryptoRank. Much of Kalshi's September growth is linked to sports-linked combinations.

At Robinhood, prediction markets have out-earned crypto for two quarters in a row. At Coinbase, prediction markets and derivatives together now account for about a quarter of transaction revenue.

Derivatives also took a larger share of exchange activity as spot turnover fell. They accounted for 83% of total exchange volume in Q3, according to TokenInsight. Separately, open interest on perpetual futures rose 40.6% over the quarter to more than $100 billion.

The Market Remained Below Its 2025 Level

The Q3 rally followed three consecutive quarters of decline in crypto market capitalisation. Bitcoin had lost about a third of its value between January and June. Total crypto market value closed September at $2.96 trillion, still 4% down for the year.

According to Coingecko reports, ayear earlier it stood at $4 trillion, while bitcoin ended September 2025 near $114,000, compared with about $83,500 this September.

The third quarter confirmed that the traditional retail crypto playbook has fractured. In previous cycles, a 40% market surge would have triggered record onboarding and retail churn. In 2026, user bases grew, but transactions languished as capital migrated into ETFs, prediction markets, and perpetuals.

Incoming fourth-quarter trading data will show whether retail investors were simply late to the rebound or whether the spot trading appetite has structurally cooled.

title: Bitcoin Price Holds Near $65,000 as Nvidia Turmoil Drags Nasdaq Down 2.5%
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Holds Near $65,000 as Nvidia Turmoil Drags Nasdaq Down 2.5%
Bitcoin price held near $65,000 on Monday afternoon, shrugging off a 2.5% Nasdaq slide as Nvidia's board ruled out bringing back Jensen Huang and the dollar hit a 19-month high.
This post Bitcoin Price Holds ...
content:
Bitcoin price traded near $65,000 on Monday afternoon, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, up more than 1% from where it sat at the time of this morning’s report. The world’s largest cryptocurrency held its ground even as a fresh round of selling in Nvidia dragged the Nasdaq down about 2.5%.

The session was choppy. Bitcoin started the day near $64,000 after a weekend plunge to $62,000, then jumped to about $65,600 shortly after the U.S. stock market opened. The bounce faded within the hour, and the bitcoin price slipped back toward $64,000 as tech stocks extended their losses. Buyers stepped in there, and bitcoin has spent most of the afternoon trading around $65,000.

Nvidia drags tech stocks lower while the bitcoin price steadies

Nvidia was again the heaviest weight on markets. CNBC reported shortly after noon that the chipmaker’s board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO after he resigned last week. The board is instead focused on an investigation into whether Huang’s conduct compromised national security or company secrets, the report said. Earlier Monday, President Donald Trump said he would not mind seeing Huang return.

Nvidia shares fell to a fresh intraday low after the report and closed down about 4%, a day before the company reports quarterly results. U.S. chipmakers dropped more than 5%. The Nasdaq Composite slid about 2.5% and the S&P 500 lost nearly 2%, with investors also bracing for Anthropic’s IPO later this week.

Bitcoin did not follow stocks to their lows this time. As the Nasdaq sank to its worst levels of the day after the CNBC report, bitcoin stopped going down and held near $64,800. That marks a change from the past week, when the bitcoin price traded largely in step with chip stocks.

Dollar hits 19-month high as Warsh stays quiet on rates

The macro backdrop offered no relief. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking at a San Francisco Fed conference, avoided any guidance on the near-term path of rates. He said artificial intelligence could lift productivity but “could bring substantial labor market disruption as some jobs are displaced, rather than complemented, by technology.”

His remarks did little to change expectations for a rate hike next month. Fed funds futures imply a quarter-point increase in December, and the dollar index touched its highest level since April 2025. A stronger dollar tends to weigh on bitcoin and gold, and gold fell to its lowest level since October 2025 earlier in the session. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.12%.

Bitcoin-linked stocks took a heavier hit than the coin itself. Strategy (MSTR) fell nearly 8% and Coinbase (COIN) dropped about 6%, while Strive (ASST), which bought 251 bitcoin last week, slid about 12%. Strategy also added 485 bitcoin last week, but it faces about $2.8 billion of potential index-fund selling when MSCI removes it at the Nov. 30 close, JPMorgan estimates. Spot bitcoin ETFs shed $185 million on Friday, their seventh straight day of outflows.

Nvidia earnings next for the bitcoin price

The next test arrives Tuesday after the bell, when Nvidia reports its fiscal third-quarter results. Analysts expect earnings growth of 90% on revenue of $109 billion. Minutes from the Fed’s October meeting follow on Wednesday, the same day Anthropic is expected to price its IPO.

For now, bitcoin has bounced twice from the $64,000 area on Monday. A move above this morning’s high near $65,600 would put Sunday’s bounce toward $66,000 back in view, while a break below today’s low near $63,800 would bring the weekend low around $62,000 back into play.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $65,000.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

Strive added 251 Bitcoin for $17.5 million as it continues expanding one of the largest corporate BTC treasuries. The purchase was partly backed by fresh preferred-stock funding, highlighting how crypto treasury companies are using increasingly complex capital structures to keep buying through the downturn.

Key Takeaways

  • Strive bought 251 BTC for $17.5M, lifting its treasury to 43,404 BTC.
  • Preferred-stock funding lets Strive keep buying bitcoin without issuing common shares.
  • The strategy now depends on servicing a 15% dividend through a prolonged crypto downturn.

Strive Boosts Bitcoin Buying Pace With 251 BTC Buy

Strive is buying the bitcoin dip, and it is increasingly leaning on preferred equity to fund the strategy.

The Nasdaq-listed company acquired 251 BTC for $17.5 million between Nov. 7 and Nov. 13 at an average price of $69,853 per bitcoin, including fees and expenses. The purchase lifted its holdings from 43,153 BTC to 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday regulatory filing, currently valued above $2.8 billion at bitcoin’s recent price near $65,000.

At the same time, Strive raised $10.02 million by selling 104,478 shares of its SATS preferred stock through an at-the-market program. It sold no common stock during the period.

Preferred Shares Become a Bitcoin Funding Engine

SATS carries a 15% annual dividend, making the financing more expensive than common equity but allowing Strive to raise capital without immediately issuing additional common shares.

CEO Matt Cole said Strive currently has 133 months of preferred-dividend coverage, equivalent to just over 11 years, and an “amplification ratio of 76%.”

The figures matter because corporate bitcoin strategies increasingly depend not only on BTC performance, but also on their ability to service the securities used to finance purchases.

Strive’s cash and equivalents fell by $22.3 million during the week to $465.3 million, while its 505,000-share position in Strategy’s STRC preferred stock remained unchanged.

Strive Keeps Accumulating Into Bitcoin Weakness

The latest acquisition was substantially larger than Strive’s previous weekly purchase of 29 BTC at an average price of $75,721. That shows the company increasing its buying pace as bitcoin trades well below its recent highs.

Speaking at the Cantor Convergence, Matt Cole spoke to why Strive keeps buying bitcoin while prices fall. He commented:

We’ve been a buyer throughout this entire bear market because the structure was very intentional in how we underwrote this perpetual thesis, where bitcoin could go to a penny. We have 18 months of cash reserves.

For crypto investors, the bigger story is the financing model. Strive is pairing a large bitcoin treasury with perpetual preferred securities, effectively using capital markets to expand BTC exposure while preserving its common-share count in the latest week.

That can magnify the benefits if bitcoin appreciates. It also leaves Strive with recurring dividend obligations if the crypto market remains weak.

With 43,404 BTC now on its balance sheet, Strive’s next challenge is no longer simply accumulating bitcoin. It is proving that the capital structure behind those purchases can remain durable through a prolonged downturn.

title: Bitcoin’s $60,000 Put Takes the Lead With $900 Million in Open Positions
summary: The $60,000 put has overtaken the $100,000 call on Deribit. But the eye-catching $900 million figure tells a more complicated story than a straightforward bet on a Bitcoin crash.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

The $60,000 put has overtaken the $100,000 call on Deribit. But the eye-catching $900 million figure tells a more complicated story than a straightforward bet on a Bitcoin crash.

Bitcoin options traders have a new focal point: the $60,000 put strike, where approximately $900 million in outstanding notional positions has overtaken the once-dominant $100,000 call.

The change, reported by CoinDesk on November 16 using Deribit data, captures a market paying closer attention to downside protection after Bitcoin’s recent slide. The $100,000 call stood at about $867 million in open interest in the same snapshot.

Yet the headline needs care. A large outstanding put position is neither $900 million freshly spent on a crash bet nor a forecast that Bitcoin must fall below $60,000. Understanding the difference is central to reading the signal.

Bitcoin options: the protection trade moves into view

Nicolas Quatravaux, Paradigm’s head of EMEA, told CoinDesk: “OI is a stock, not a flow.” He attributed the change in ranking partly to traders closing bullish $100,000 calls, rather than a uniform rush into downside contracts.

That explanation changes the story. A defensive position can move to the top because another position shrinks. The ranking alone cannot show how much fresh fear entered the market that day, or how many investors changed their outlook.

The figures are a dated snapshot of outstanding exposure. They should not be read as a live order book, a single trader’s position or a scheduled sale of the underlying cryptocurrency.

Open interest counts contracts, not convictions

The Options Industry Council’s explanation of open interest separates outstanding contracts from session trading volume. When both counterparties open positions, open interest increases; when both close, it falls. A position changing hands can leave the count unchanged.

Consider a hypothetical transfer of ten contracts from an existing holder to a new buyer, with the other side staying open. Trading activity has occurred, but the market has not necessarily added ten new outstanding contracts. Confusing those measurements can exaggerate a shift in sentiment.

Every contract also has two sides. The buyer may want protection, while the seller may be collecting a premium or offsetting another exposure. The public total does not disclose either participant’s complete portfolio.

For a Bitcoin holder, buying protection can be consistent with keeping the coins. For an investor with several option legs, a put may be only one component of a strategy. Counting it as an isolated bearish vote loses that context.

A $60,000 strike is not a price target

Deribit’s contract specifications explain that its inverse BTC options represent one Bitcoin per contract. A put provides exposure to selling at its strike, with the eventual result determined under the exchange’s settlement rules.

The contract’s notional size describes the underlying exposure. Its premium is the separate price paid for the option. Treating the two as interchangeable can turn a large market exposure into a misleading claim about cash committed.

The strike also differs from the buyer’s break-even point. In a simplified dollar-denominated example, a $60,000 put bought for a $2,000 premium would require a settlement price below $58,000 to show a net expiry profit before fees. Those are illustrative numbers, not a quote for an available contract.

A settlement below $60,000 would give that hypothetical put intrinsic value, but would not automatically recover its purchase cost. For a hedger, however, limiting losses on a larger holding could matter more than the option’s standalone return.

Expiry dates can change the interpretation

Deribit’s guide to its metrics shows that open interest can be viewed across all expirations or filtered by a particular expiry. Its tools also separate outstanding positions from 24-hour put and call trading volumes.

That distinction matters because a near-term hedge and one extending months ahead answer different questions. Aggregating them at the same strike can reveal a popular protection level while obscuring when that protection is intended to apply.

A stronger assessment would compare matching expirations, changes in contract counts and prices paid for protection. Otherwise, a large but old position can overshadow a smaller, more informative new trade.

Changes in dollar notional also need a consistent valuation basis. If a dataset converts outstanding coin exposure using the prevailing Bitcoin price, the dollar amount can move even without an equivalent change in the number of contracts. Comparing like-for-like contract counts helps avoid that trap.

Compare derivatives with actual buying and selling

BNC’s report on two weeks of Bitcoin ETF withdrawals examined a separate measure: net money entering or leaving investment products. Options exposure and ETF flows can complement each other, but describe different activities.

An investor may retain fund shares while adding a hedge, or reduce spot exposure while closing an option. Without linked account data, those choices cannot be reconstructed from two aggregate headlines.

For readers watching the next move, the useful question is whether fresh defensive demand continues alongside weak spot buying. A reversal in either could change the picture. The $60,000 strike is a meaningful location to monitor; its prominence does not settle Bitcoin’s destination.

title: Bitmine edges toward 5% of ETH supply as treasuries report buys amid market slump
summary: Strategy, Strive, Bitmine and Cypherpunk disclosed fresh additions to their crypto treasuries, spanning Bitcoin, Ether and Zcash.
content:
Publicly traded crypto treasury companies Bitmine, Strive and Cypherpunk Technologies disclosed increases in their cryptocurrency holdings on Monday, joining Strategy in accumulating digital assets despite a broader market downturn.

Bitmine, the largest publicly traded Ether treasury company, said it added 7,653 Ether (ETH) over the past week, bringing its total holdings to 6.08 million ETH, about 4.97% of its total supply and bringing it ever closer to its stated aim of accumulating 5% of the ETH supply, according to a Monday announcement.

Top Bitcoin treasury companies Strategy and Strive also reported purchases. Strategy acquired 485 Bitcoin (BTC) for $33.4 million, while Strive bought 251 BTC for $17.5 million, bringing its holdings to 43,404 BTC — just 110 BTC behind Twenty One Capital, the third-largest publicly traded Bitcoin holder, according to BitcoinTreasuries.net data.

Zcash (ZEC) treasury and mining company Cypherpunk Technologies reported buying 3,775.72 ZEC for $3.48 million since September and mining another 5,721.35 ZEC in October. The additions brought its holdings to 341,858.75 ZEC, or around 2% of circulating supply.

The purchases come amid a broader cryptocurrency sell-off. Bitcoin was trading around $65,017, down 12.9% over the past seven days and 20% over the past month. ETH fell 14.2% and ZEC dropped 22.9% over the past week, according to CoinGecko data as of 8:08 pm UTC on Monday.

Bitcoin is down around 20% over the past month. Source: CoinGecko

title: Senate Agriculture Committee to Hear Trump’s CFTC Nominees Tuesday
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Senate Agriculture Committee to Hear Trump’s CFTC Nominees Tuesday
The Senate Agriculture Committee will hear Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland on Tuesday, President Trump's bipartisan picks to join CFTC Chairman Michael Selig, currently the agency's only sitting commissioner.
Thi...
content:
The Senate Agriculture Committee will hear President Donald Trump’s two nominees to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on Tuesday, a confirmation hearing that comes as the derivatives regulator has only one sitting commissioner.

The committee scheduled the session for 3 p.m. Eastern in Room 106 of the Dirksen Senate Office Building. The White House sent the nominations to the Senate on Nov. 12. The nominees are Nathan Anonick of Virginia and Matthew Rowland of the District of Columbia. The hearing notice says to check back for live video, and the committee has not posted written testimony.

Trump nominated the pair last week as part of a bipartisan slate for the CFTC and the Securities and Exchange Commission, a step that would begin to refill two regulators that have been operating short-handed.

Who the nominees are

Anonick serves on the Republican staff of the Senate Agriculture Committee under Chairman John Boozman of Arkansas. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. A 2023 committee release said Anonick joined the panel in 2022 to manage a portfolio that includes cryptocurrencies, futures markets and derivatives, and that he had previously worked at the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation as a resolution policy specialist.

Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee’s Democratic staff under Ranking Member Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer K. Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both nominees come from the committee that oversees the CFTC.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” and said he looks forward to working with them “upon their confirmation by the US Senate.”

Kristin N. Johnson and Steven Levine, the two SEC nominees from the same White House list, are on the agenda for a Senate Banking Committee nominations hearing at 10 a.m. Thursday in Dirksen 538.

A CFTC commission of one

The CFTC can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from the same party. Chairman Michael S. Selig, sworn in Dec. 22, 2025, is currently the only sitting commissioner listed on the agency’s website. Even if the Senate confirms both nominees, two of the five seats would remain vacant.

Each nominee still needs a committee vote and then confirmation by the full Senate. The Agriculture Committee has not scheduled that vote.

A lame-duck clock and a stalled Clarity Act

The hearing lands in a lame-duck Senate, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. The new Congress is seated in January. If the Senate does not confirm the nominations before then, they would typically be returned to the president and have to be sent again.

After the election, TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg told clients he does not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees unless the president fills Democratic seats at agencies such as the FDIC and the SEC, a step he has called unlikely. The White House slate does that at both the SEC and the CFTC.

The nominations also arrive with crypto market structure legislation stalled. The Clarity Act failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and dies on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it. The bill would formally divide oversight of digital assets between the SEC and the CFTC, distinguishing which are securities, commodities or stablecoins.

Without new law, the CFTC has set much of its crypto policy on its own this year. Selig’s agency opened the door to equity perpetual futures, and a federal judge later said the CFTC likely overstepped its authority while letting trading continue.

The open question is whether a Senate heading for Democratic control confirms the CFTC picks before January, or leaves the agency short-handed into 2027.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Revolut Placed Under Court Supervision in Italy After Failing to Flag Criminal Funds
summary:
An Italian court has placed Revolut’s local branch, Revolut Bank UAB, under judicial administration for one year and ordered external supervision of its anti-money laundering controls.
The digital bank failed to flag tens of millions of euros moved by convicted criminals. The judicial intervention m...
content:
2026-11-16T22:26:00.000+02:00

Monday, 16/11/2026 | 20:26 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Reuters reported that 24 people moved or concealed €41.9 million through Revolut accounts between 2021 and 2026.
  • Revolut’s US CEO acknowledged that the court action could affect its pending US banking licence.

An Italian court has placed Revolut’s local branch, Revolut Bank UAB, under judicial administration for one year and ordered external supervision of its anti-money laundering controls.

The digital bank failed to flag tens of millions of euros moved by convicted criminals. The judicial intervention may complicate its long-standing bid for a coveted US national bank charter, Reuters reports.

Two court-appointed administrators will oversee improvements to its Italian controls alongside existing management. Revolut said its retail and business banking services in the country continue normally.

Court Focuses on Missed Suspicious Activity

According to the ruling reviewed by Reuters, 24 people under investigation or convicted of serious crimes moved or concealed €41.9 million through Revolut accounts between 2021 and 2026. Other banks filed 265 suspicious transaction reports concerning those individuals during the period; Revolut filed none.

Meanwhile, according to estimates cited by Milan Chief Prosecutor Marcello Viola, deficiencies in Revolut's operating model might have facilitated the transfer of €76.5 million in illicit funds. Prosecutors believe that the bank could have detected all those transactions with standard AML procedures.

Judicial administration is a preventive measure intended to examine how the bank verifies customers and monitors transactions, and to correct controls where necessary. Administrators won’t take on day-to-day management. Revolut itself is not under criminal investigation in this case, Reuters reports.

Separate Reviews Add to the Pressure

The UIF, the Bank of Italy's anti-money laundering arm, is conducting a separate investigation. While Milan prosecutors use Italy’s Anti-Mafia Code to ensure the bank is not used by organised crime, the UIF inspection is a supervisory audit focused on technical compliance with existing rules and regulations.

In April 2025, the Bank of Lithuania initiated AML action against Revolut Bank UAB. The regulator found shortcomings in its monitoring of customer relationships and transactions, and fined the bank €3.5 million.

The Italian decision comes as Revolut awaits approval of its application for a US bank charter. Asked about possible effects beyond Italy, US CEO Cetin Duransoy said: “If you would have a massive hiccup somewhere, it's going to have an impact in other places.”

Revolut must submit a plan to address the Italian control failures within 60 days. The court-appointed administrators will assess whether its customer checks and transaction monitoring can identify the activity the court says they missed.

title: Boris Johnson says UK must lead blockchain development despite crypto doubts
summary: Johnson was joined by Lord Ross Kempsell who called for regulators to work with industry participants to bring the UK to the forefront.
content:
Former United Kingdom Prime Minister Boris Johnson has backed blockchain technology and tokenization as opportunities for the UK’s financial sector, despite persistent doubts about cryptocurrencies. 

Speaking at Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London on Monday, Johnson maintained his position that Bitcoin (BTC) resembles a Ponzi scheme, following an opinion piece published in the Daily Mail in March. He questioned who investors could hold accountable if funds were stolen.

However, Johnson distinguished his criticism of digital assets from his view of the underlying technology, saying the UK should be at the forefront of tokenization. 

Lord Ross Kempsell, who joined Johnson on stage, said although he shared his reservations on cryptocurrencies, “on the parts of the industry that can be brought into a regulated perimeter, which the regulators are working on, there’s a lot of scope here for a high growth industry.”

Lord Kempsell pushes for regulators’ collaboration with market

Kempsell, whom Johnson nominated for a peerage in 2022, told the panel that more than 8% of UK adults hold crypto, in line with Financial Conduct Authority-commissioned research published in December 2025.  Speaking to Cointelegraph after his stage appearance, he said, “I’m a very big believer in making London and keeping London as the onchain capital for innovation.”

Related: UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws

He argued that consumer protection and financial innovation should not be treated as competing priorities, pointing to the UK’s established fintech industry as an example of how regulation can coexist with innovation in the country. He said the UK should avoid introducing a single, all-encompassing piece of crypto legislation, opting instead for “a more ad-hoc approach” to regulation. 

He called for collaboration between the regulators and market participants to understand both the risks and opportunities. While he saw consumer protection as “paramount,” he felt it was unfair to single out the crypto industry as the only sector where consumer protection was at risk. 

“Really what I care about is the economic growth potential that there is in this industry, the job creation potential, and also its wider links to tech, AI and traditional financial innovation. London’s always been at the center of those historically,” Kempsell told Cointelegraph. 

When asked about the approach of the current administration in the UK, he highlighted that “they need to make sure that they get the fundamental market conditions right.” In his eyes, that meant making the UK a competitive player in regard to tax and facilitating business innovation. 

Related: UK names 6 banks to lead first digitally native government bond

Industry points to market infrastructure

Tim Meggs, co-founder of London-based digital asset trading firm Lo:Tech, said Johnson “made a fair point about people getting burned,” but said most of the losses experienced by the industry stemmed from thin liquidity and a lack of visibility over how prices were made.

“If the FCA gets its perimeter right, the UK has a chance to make that kind of transparency the norm,” Meggs said. “But until the clearing and prime broking infrastructure catches up, good rules won’t be enough on their own to make London the place where serious digital asset trading gets done.”

Robin Nordnes, founder and CEO of Solana infrastructure firm Raiku, argued that Johnson’s question about who is in charge makes the case for blockchain, since a public ledger needs no guarantor. “Every transaction on Solana is public and can be checked by anyone, which is more than you can say for most of what happens in the City,” he said.

Nordnes warned that “if Westminster keeps treating this as retail speculation, the trading systems behind the next generation of markets will be built in New York and Singapore, and London will end up renting them.”

title: RZR Funded Adds Prediction-Market Challenges after Hantec Trader Rebrand
summary:
RZR Funded (the former Hantec Trader) have launched one-stage prediction market challenges as an extension of their simulated trading model which previously covered currencies, indices and commodities.


The launch is aimed at people who follow the elections, the football or the economic decisions b...
content:
2026-11-16T21:06:50.230+02:00

Monday, 16/11/2026 | 19:06 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • RZR Funded now lets participants complete one-stage simulated prop challenges using prediction markets.
  • Prices follow external prediction markets, but no real contracts are traded.

RZR Funded (the former Hantec Trader) have launched one-stage prediction market challenges as an extension of their simulated trading model which previously covered currencies, indices and commodities.

The new product enables participants to take virtual positions on over 5,000 events across politics, sport, economics, crypto and weather. Those who pass the screening will be awarded a simulated funded account and may be eligible for cash rewards based on their virtual profits.
