In November 2023, Binance and its CEO, CZ, pleaded guilty to unlicensed money transmitting and anti-money laundering violations charges. This happened a month after Binance paused all U.S. dollar deposits, withdrawals, and trades in response to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) lawsuit filed against Binance.US on June 5, 2023.
  • Custodial Risk: Although Binance offers self‑custody through its Web3 wallet, most of the users keep their funds on the exchange for trading. In November 2022 and October 2023, there were hacks against the BNB Chain (around $570 million), and earlier in 2019, hackers stole about 7,000 BTC from the exchange. Obviously, Binance covered the losses through the SAFU fund, but these incidents eventually show that even big exchanges are not immune to security breaches.

Who Is Binance Best For?

Binance is best for active day traders, altcoin investors, passive income, high-volume traders, and tech-savvy beginners.

  • Active traders: People who trade often and require deep liquidity, low fees, and sophisticated tools. You see, the large selection of pairs, high leverage, and advanced order types can easily attract day traders and professional investors.
  • Altcoin enthusiasts: Generally, those looking to buy or sell lesser‑known cryptocurrencies or take part in new token launches through the Launchpad will find more options on Binance than on most competitors.
  • Yield seekers: If you want to earn passive income on your crypto, Binance offers numerous staking, lending, and yield farming products with competitive returns.
  • High‑volume traders: VIP tier programs reward high trading volumes with lower fees and better borrowing rates. Plus, corporations or trading firms can also open institutional accounts with dedicated support and portfolio margin programs.
  • Tech‑savvy beginners: It has the Lite interface and educational resources like Binance Academy, so new users can start with simple buys and gradually explore more advanced products.

If Binance fits your trading goals, open your account today and activate your referral bonus before placing your first trade.

What are Binance Fees?

The Binance fees include spot trading charges (0.1% maker/taker), futures trading fees (0.02% maker, 0.05% taker), zero deposit fees, and variable withdrawal fees (depending on the network).

Deposit Fees

The platform generally does not charge you any fees to deposit cryptocurrency into your account. You only have to pay the network fee to the blockchain when you send the coins from your personal wallet.  Unlike crypto deposits, fiat deposits involve third-party payment providers. The table below summarizes the core fees for retail users (both crypto and fiat deposit fees):

Deposit methodBinance Global
Bank transfer (SEPA, FPS, ACH)Free for most currencies. SEPA bank deposit is usually free; Faster Payments Service (FPS) in the UK is free.
Debit/credit cardCard deposits cost around 1.8-2% of the amount. Apple Pay and Google Pay have similar rates
Third‑party payments (Simplex, Banxa, etc.)Fees vary by service, typically around 1-3%
Crypto depositFree; network miners’ fee paid by sender

Withdrawal Fees

Binance crypto withdrawal fees are not fixed, and they change based on which coin you are moving and how busy the network is. You will find that withdrawing Bitcoin usually costs a $5-$10, but withdrawing tokens on the BNB Chain (previously Binance Smart Chain) or Solana can cost less than 50 cents. Actually, the exchange updates these rates regularly to make sure they match the actual blockchain costs.

Withdrawal methodBinance Global
Bank transferSEPA withdrawals cost around €1-€1.50; wire transfers cost $15; some regions are free.
Debit/credit cardNot available for withdrawals.
Crypto withdrawalOnly the network fee is charged

Spot Trading Fees

Binance spot trading charges are based on a tiered system, from regular users to VIP 9. Now, for regular users, a 0.10% maker and taker fee is charged for spot trading. 

Your fees reduce slightly if you are trading USDC. Makers still pay the standard rate, but takers pay 0.095%. If you increase your trading volume over 30 days or hold a significant amount of BNB in your account, your spot trading fees will drop to as low as 0.011% / 0.023% maker-taker. (check screenshot below for exact discount details and VIP tiers)

Futures Trading Fees

Futures trading has a separate fee schedule because the volumes are usually much larger than spot trading. Makers, who provide liquidity to the book, pay as little as 0.02%, while takers pay around 0.05%. You also get a 10% discount on futures fees if you pay using your BNB balance. Right now, these are some of the lowest derivatives fees you can find on any major centralized exchange.

Margin Trading Fees

Binance margin trading has two cost components: trading commission (same as spot rates) and interest on borrowed funds. These rates change every single day based on how many people are borrowing that specific coin. Generally, USDT interest rates might be around 5% to 10% per year, while smaller altcoins might be much more expensive.

Staking and Earn Fees

The Binance platform does not usually charge a direct fee for you to participate in staking or the Earn programs. But instead, the company takes a small percentage of the rewards that the blockchain pays out before they give you your share. So, this means the APY (Annual Percentage Yield) you see in the app is the net amount you will actually receive. Binance.US, however, deducts a 9.95% to 39.95% service fee from staking rewards.

What Are the Best Features of Binance?

The best features of the Binance exchange are advanced trading features, staking services, launchpad, user-friendly mobile app, passive income options, web3 wallet, cloud mining, and an NFT marketplace. 

Binance Trading Features

The top Binance trading features are spot trading, margin trading, futures trading, options trading, copy trading, and automated trading bots.

Binance Margin Trading

Binance margin trading allows you to borrow funds to increase your position size. Binance offers isolated margin (up to 10x leverage), where the collateral is tied to one trading pair, and cross margin (up to 5x). There is also cross margin pro for institutional and high‑volume users that raises leverage to 20x. Higher leverage increases both potential profits and losses.

Here, margin loans generally accrue interest every hour, and rates depend on the coin you borrow (as discussed earlier). Binance also uses a “Smart Liquidation” engine that gradually reduces your positions instead of closing them all at once. There is also Portfolio Margin. It lets you use combined balances across spot, margin, and futures to lower margin requirements and support large leveraged trades.

Binance Spot Trading

Binance spot trading means you can buy and sell crypto directly with market or limit orders. Spot trading pairs include crypto‑crypto pairs (e.g., BTC/ETH), crypto‑fiat pairs (e.g., ETH/EUR), and stablecoin pairs (e.g., BNB/USDT). 

The interface allows you to view order book depth, price charts, and trade history. Generally, spot trades settle immediately, and you own the underlying asset.

Now, if you are a more advanced trader, Binance provides more advanced features for the spot market to support order types and charting features. These features allow you to set limits, market, stop-limit orders, and more. You can read our in-depth Binance spot trading review for more info.

Binance Futures Trading

Binance futures trading lets you bet on whether the price of a coin will go up or down without actually owning the coin itself. It offers USDT‑margined perpetual contracts, coin‑margined perpetual contracts, and delivery futures with expiry dates. 

You can use much higher leverage here, sometimes up to 125x for certain pairs. Binance also provides tools such as isolated and cross margin for futures, take‑profit and stop‑loss orders, bracket orders, and a risk calculator. Check out our Binance futures review article for more details.

Binance Options Trading

Binance options trading gives you the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a coin at a certain price before a certain date. You can trade European‑style options settled in USDT, and these options have a set strike price and expiry time. The platform has a very simplified options interface that makes it easier to understand than the ones used in traditional stock markets. 

Now, because they are European options, you cannot exercise early, and the platform also offers a simple options widget called “Vanilla Options” for beginner use. 

Binance Copy Trading

Binance copy trading allows you to follow the strategies of other experienced traders. Basically, you can choose a lead trader, allocate funds, and then the system automatically mirrors their trades. 

Here, lead traders earn a 10-30 % share of the profits, and they must maintain consistent performance to remain in the program. You can copy in two ways: fixed amount, where you invest a specific sum, and fixed ratio, where your position sizes follow the same ratio as the lead trader’s positions. 

There is also an “Elite Trader Program” that requires at least 300 copy traders and $750,000 in assets under management. Copy trading supports both spot and futures markets. Also, you can stop copying at any time and withdraw your funds. There are no restrictions.

Binance Trading Bot

Binance offers built-in bots that can trade for you 24/7 based on rules you set. Here are some top Binance trading bots:

  • Spot Grid Bot: This one can place buy and sell orders around a set price range, profiting from sideways markets by buying low and selling high.
  • Futures Grid Bot: Similar to spot grid but for perpetual contracts. So, it will use leverage.
  • Arbitrage Bot: It will exploit price differences between funding rates or futures and spot prices.
  • Rebalancing Bot: This bot generally keeps your portfolio balanced by periodically adjusting allocations to maintain target ratios. You can set the coins and percentage distribution, and the bot rebalances at regular intervals or when price thresholds are met.
  • Auto‑Invest Bot: Implements dollar cost averaging by automatically buying selected coins at fixed intervals. You can choose daily, weekly, or monthly frequency and have the option to earn interest on unspent stablecoins.
  • Spot DCA Bot: This bot buys increments of a coin when the price drops by a set percentage and sells increments when the price rises by a set percentage. It helps manage volatility.
  • Futures TWAP/VP Bots: The bot will execute large orders over time using time‑weighted average price (TWAP) or volume participation (VP) strategies to minimize market impact.

Binance Staking

Binance staking allows you to earn rewards just by holding certain coins in your account. The platform handles all the technical work, and you just click a button to start earning interest. You can choose “Locked Staking” for higher returns if you don’t mind locking your coins there for a set time, or “Flexible Staking” if you want to be able to withdraw them whenever you want.

Binance takes a 10% cut of rewards on popular coins such as Ethereum and Solana. There is also ETH 2.0 liquid staking, which provides a token called WBETH that represents your staked ETH and accrues staking rewards. Explore our Binance staking review article for more info. 

Binance Launchpad

Binance Launchpad is a platform for new cryptocurrency projects to raise capital through token sales. You can participate by holding BNB in your account. The number of tokens you can buy depends on your average BNB holdings over a snapshot period (often 7–30 days) and the project’s allocation rules. 

Binance calculates your ticket based on hourly snapshots of your BNB balance, and at the end of the subscription period, winning tickets are drawn, and BNB is deducted from your wallet to purchase the new tokens. Check out our full Binance launchpad review here.

Binance Mobile App

The Binance mobile app offers two modes: Lite for beginners and Pro for experienced traders. The Lite version displays simple buy/sell options, price charts, and a portfolio overview. The Pro version provides full order books, margin and futures trading, advanced charting, and access to copy trading, bots, and Earn. 

The app also integrates with the Web3 wallet, so you can access DeFi and NFTs within the same interface. It has all the top security features, like biometric login (fingerprint/face), device management, anti‑phishing codes, and the ability to freeze your account from the app.

Binance Earn

Binance Earn is basically a high-yield savings account for your crypto. You can put your coins into various products like “Simple Earn” or “Dual Investment” to get a better return than just letting them HODL in your wallet. Now, within Earn, you will find:

  • Simple Earn: Flexible and locked staking as explained earlier.
  • Launchpool: You can stake BNB or stablecoins to farm new tokens.
  • Dual Investment: You can earn a fixed yield by committing crypto or stablecoins to a price target. Here, if the price is above the target at expiry, you receive your crypto plus yield in stablecoins; if below, you receive more crypto plus yield. It suits users comfortable with market exposure.

Binance Web3 Wallet

Binance Web3 Wallet is a self‑custodial cryptocurrency wallet built into the Binance mobile app. The wallet uses multi‑party computation (MPC). Here, your private key is split into multiple shares. So, one share stays on your device, one stays on Binance’s servers, and the last one is saved in your personal cloud (such as iCloud or Google Drive). 

Now, you need at least two shares to sign a transaction, so neither you nor Binance can move funds alone. The wallet supports multiple blockchains, including BNB Chain, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, and more. It also has a dApp browser so you can interact with DeFi, yield farms, NFT platforms, and games within the app. Here is the full Binance Web3 wallet review.

Binance Cloud Mining

Binance cloud mining allows you to earn Bitcoin (BTC) without having to buy expensive mining hardware yourself. You basically rent the “hash power” from the platform’s massive data centers, and they send the rewards to your account every day. This is a great way to get into mining if you live in a place where electricity is expensive or if you don’t have space for loud machines. You can read our in-depth Binance cloud mining review to know more.

Binance NFT Marketplace

Binance has its own marketplace where you can buy, sell, and even create your own Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). You can find digital art, gaming items, and collectibles from creators all over the world. The platform supports BEP‑721 and BEP‑1155 standards on the BNB Chain. You can check out the full Binance NFT marketplace review for more details.

How to Open a Trading Account at Binance Global Exchange?

Step 1: Click the “Open Account” button below to start Binance or download the Binance app, and register your Binance account using your email address, mobile phone number, Google account, or Apple ID.

Step 2: Check the “agree with Binance terms of service and privacy policy”, and click “Next” to proceed. Binance will then send a verification code to the email or phone number you added. Enter the code number and click Submit.

Step 3: At this step, you need to create a strong password (at least 8 characters, including uppercase letters and numbers).

Step 4: If you didn’t use the registration link in step one, add our Binance referral code here manually to get rewards. This code can give you up to $100 in a free crypto sign-up bonus. After that, Binance will ask you to complete your verification. Click “Continue” to start the verification process.

Step 5: Finally, once you finish the KYC verification process, it can generally take a few hours to two days to have your account verified and ready for use.

Follow the steps above and register your Binance account now to claim up to $100 in crypto rewards.

How to Deposit to Your Binance Trading Account?

To deposit fiat on Binance, you need to go to the “Deposit” section, choose your local currency, select a payment method, enter the amount, and wait for confirmation.

To deposit crypto on Binance, you need to select the cryptocurrency, copy the deposit address, and send the funds from your external wallet.

Fiat Deposits

  • Choose your currency: Log in, go to Wallet > Fiat and Spot > Deposit, then select your local currency (USD, EUR, GBP, INR, etc.).
  • Select a payment method: You can choose bank transfer (SEPA, SWIFT, ACH, FPS), card deposit, or third‑party services. Now, for example, if you are in India, you might use IMPS or a UPI transfer; in Europe, you would use SEPA; in the US, you can use ACH or a debit card (available only on Binance US).
  • Enter the amount: Now, you need to type how much you want to deposit and follow the instructions to complete the transfer. Here, for card deposits, you will be redirected to the payment processor, and bank transfers require you to send money to a Binance bank account with your reference code.
  • Wait for confirmation: Generally, bank transfers may take hours or days; card deposits are instant. Once funds arrive, you will see them in your Fiat and Spot wallet.

Crypto Deposits

  • Choose the crypto: Go to Wallet > Fiat and Spot > Deposit, then select your desired coin (e.g., BTC, ETH, USDT).
  • Select network: Binance generally supports multiple networks for many coins, so for instance, USDT can be deposited via Ethereum (ERC‑20), BNB Chain (BEP‑20), Tron (TRC‑20), or Arbitrum. 
  • Copy the deposit address: Binance generates an address, so you need to copy it and paste it into the sending wallet. Also, some coins require a memo or tag (e.g., for XRP, XLM), and if you forget the memo, your deposit may be delayed. So, check that too.
  • Send the funds: Now, you can initiate the transfer from your external wallet, and after network confirmations, the deposit will appear in your Binance wallet. Well, deposits are usually credited after one or two confirmations for major coins; smaller networks may take longer.

How to Trade on Binance?

To trade on Binance, you can start with the “Convert” feature if you want to swap coins without looking at charts, and for more control, you should use the “Spot Trading” interface, which gives you access to the full order book.

  • Find the “Trade” menu and select “Spot.”
  • Search for the pair you want to trade, like BTC/USDT, on the right side of the screen.
  • Choose between a “Market” order to buy immediately at the current price or a “Limit” order to set your own price.
  • Enter the amount of crypto you want to buy and click the large green “Buy” button. Actually, you can also set “Stop-Loss” orders to protect your money if you think the price may drop too fast.

How to Withdraw from Binance?

To withdraw from Binance, go to the “withdraw” section, choose coin, paste the withdrawal address, select the network and amount, and finally confirm the transaction. 

  • Navigate to your wallet and select the “Withdraw” option.
  • Enter the destination address of your private wallet and pick the matching network.
  • Type in the amount of crypto you want to move.
  • Confirm the transaction and wait for the blockchain to process it. Generally, most withdrawals take between 5 and 20 minutes to complete.

What are the Available Cryptocurrencies on Binance?

There are currently over 500 cryptocurrencies available on Binance. You can generally find everything from the top-rated coins that everyone knows to small experimental projects (mostly on Binance Alpha).

  • Top Assets: You can trade Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL) with massive volume.
  • Stablecoins: The platform supports USDT, USDC, and its own FDUSD stablecoin for safekeeping.
  • Ecosystem Tokens: You can buy BNB, which powers the entire ecosystem and gives you fee discounts.
  • Meme Coins: You can find popular tokens like DOGE, PEPE, and SHIB listed with high liquidity.
  • DeFi and AI Coins: The exchange lists hundreds of project tokens for Artificial Intelligence and decentralized finance.

Binance Security Review: Is It a Safe and Legit Crypto Exchange to Trade?

Yes, Binance is a legit and safe crypto exchange. It uses industry‑standard security measures and has a large insurance fund. Here are its most advanced security systems:

  • Proof of Reserves (PoR): Binance publishes Merkle tree proofs showing that the exchange holds reserves equal to users’ balances. So, you can verify your own balances on the PoR page by generating a leaf of the Merkle tree, and the audit covers major assets like BTC, ETH, USDT, and BNB.
  • Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU): Binance created the SAFU in 2018. It is an insurance fund seeded with trading fees and acts as a backstop in case of hacks or extreme events. Currently, at the time of writing, Binance converted SAFU holdings to BTC, worth about $1 billion. The company pledged to top up the fund if its value falls below $800 million.
  • Cold storage: The majority of user funds on Binance are kept in cold wallets not connected to the internet, and only a small portion remains in hot wallets for daily withdrawals.
  • Risk engine: Binance uses an automated risk engine to monitor accounts and block suspicious activity. Basically, it includes real‑time transaction monitoring, geofencing, and anti‑money laundering (AML) procedures.
  • Withdrawal whitelisting: Binance also has an address whitelisting feature that restricts withdrawals to only pre-approved addresses. When you enable this feature, your account can only send funds to these whitelisted addresses. This will prevent unauthorized access and losses in a phishing attack or hack.

Trade with confidence on a platform backed by Proof of Reserves and a $1B SAFU fund — create your Binance account today.

But yes, Binance has also faced many regulatory issues in various countries. But besides regulatory issues, it has also been involved in scandals and significant lawsuits, like the one filed against Binance.US by the SEC in June 2023. 

Also, Binance and its CEO, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to anti-money laundering violations and other charges on November 21, 2023. Binance agreed to pay $4.3 billion to settle charges, while Changpeng Zhao stepped down as CEO and agreed to pay $50 million toward the settlement.

Can Binance be Trusted?

Yes, the Binance exchange can be trusted because it has a long history of protecting users and following international financial standards. You might hear about legal battles in the news, but the company has always worked with governments to resolve these issues and improve its systems. 

There are over 300 million registered users globally without any problems, which is obviously a very strong sign of reliability. Actually, the company has survived many “crypto winters” and market crashes while remaining the number one exchange in the world. But still, it’s a custodial platform. So, we say, use Binance for trading and short‑term storage, then transfer your long‑term holdings to a personal hardware wallet you control.

The top alternative trading platforms to Binance are Coinbase, Bybit, OKX, MEXC, and KuCoin.

title: Coinone Customer Data Breach Sparks Fresh Phishing Risk for South Korean Crypto Users
summary:
Key Takeaways: Coinone acknowledged a hack on customer support firm MetaM. There is a possibility of the sensitive user data and crypto data being exposed. Coinone states that neither its
The post Coinone Customer Data Breach Sparks Fresh Phishing Risk for South Korean Crypto Users appeared first on...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Coinone acknowledged a hack on customer support firm MetaM.
  • There is a possibility of the sensitive user data and crypto data being exposed.
  • Coinone states that neither its trading nor its wallet were directly attacked.

South Korean crypto exchange Coinone has disclosed a customer data breach linked to an outsourced support provider, raising concerns over phishing, impersonation and attempted account takeovers. According to the exchange, the incident did not withstand its fundamental trading and crypto wallet systems.

  • Coinone Breach Exposed Customer Support Data
  • Core Crypto Systems Show No Direct Compromise
    • Phishing Risk Becomes the Immediate Crypto Security Concern
    • Coinone Tightens Monitoring After the Incident

Coinone Breach Exposed Customer Support Data

The breach of servers operated by customer support provider company MetaM was made by an “external attacker,” according to Coinone, which took place around 4 a.m. Nov. 12.

Later that morning, the incident was reported to Coinone by MetaM. As part of the exchange, the hacker could inspect and/or access information in the customer service records.

Names, phone numbers, email addresses, birth dates, bank information, passwords, national ID’s, issuance dates thereof, home addresses, cryptographic wallet addresses and transaction ID’s.

The exact information affected varies per user as each customer entered different information into support conversations. Users who did not make contact with the customer service center are immune, said Coinone. No one seems to have revealed how many customers were affected by the breach at the exchange.

Read More: South Korea Gives Crypto Exchanges Power to Freeze Withdrawals on Suspected Hacks

Core Crypto Systems Show No Direct Compromise

Coinone said that customer accounts, a trading platform, and a digital asset wallet system are all separate from MetaM’s.

For now, the exchange stated it hasn’t discovered any proof those systems had been directly hacked. It also stated that the leakage information should not be enough for a hacker to log in or withdraw crypto as that needs to be done via 2FA on the Coinone account.

However, wallets where personal identification, transaction IDs, and wallet addresses are exposed would provide more convincing data for targeted attacks.

Phishing Risk Becomes the Immediate Crypto Security Concern

Coinone stated that the attackers can use the leaked data for phishing emails, service phishing, voice scam and identity theft.

The risk is especially great if the scammers do know information from a previous support session. A bogus email with reference to an actual transaction, wallet address, or some sort of customer service form could seem more serious than a random phishing scheme.

Coinone recommended users to immediately update and change the password entered for this transaction if they ever did it in another app. The exchange also disclosed that it will not request passwords, OTPs or phone, text or email codes for authentication.

Coinone Tightens Monitoring After the Incident

After the breach, Coinone identified the IP address and access link used in the attack and has transitioned customer support to emails, while investigating the matter.

The company enhanced real-time suspicious logins and transactions monitoring and is evaluating the security of its service provider. Coinone informed the Personal Information Protection Commission, Financial Supervisory Service and Korea Internet & Security Agency of the breach.

title: Ethereum (ETH) Price Prediction: $1,700 Support Holds as Falling Exchange Reserves Strengthen the Recovery Case
summary: Ethereum (ETH) price prediction remains at a critical juncture as buyers defend the $1,700 support level, while falling Binance exchange reserves strengthen hopes of a broader recovery.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

Ethereum (ETH) price prediction remains at a critical juncture as buyers defend the $1,700 support level, while falling Binance exchange reserves strengthen hopes of a broader recovery.

Ethereum is trying to recover after another sharp leg lower, with buyers stepping in around one of the more important support areas on the weekly chart. Brave New Coin data shows ETH trading around the low $1,800s after briefly falling toward $1,700, leaving the market at a point where the next reaction could shape the remainder of Q4.

The technical picture remains fragile, but there are early signs of some stabilization.

Ethereum price is trading at around $1,813, down 1.60% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

Ethereum Rebounds From the $1,700- $1,720 Support Zone

Ethereum has already tested the first major downside area highlighted on the weekly chart. Ted Pillows points to roughly $1,700-$1,720 as an important support zone, and ETH responded from that region before recovering back toward the low $1,800s.

The significance of this area goes beyond the latest bounce. ETH Price has previously reacted strongly around the same broader region, which makes the latest defense an important first step in slowing the decline. The next challenge is whether buyers can build on that reaction rather than allowing ETH to drift back toward the lows.

The first larger resistance sits around $1,965, followed by a more important zone near $2,130-$2,226. A sustained recovery through that area would improve the weekly structure considerably. If $1,700 fails instead, the chart leaves the next downside levels near $1,580 and then the broader $1,400 region.

Source: Ted Pillows via X.

Short-Term ETH Recovery Needs a Break Above $1,833

The lower-timeframe chart is beginning to improve after the latest flush. Famous crypto analyst Trader Symba highlights a strong reaction from approximately $1,772, following the earlier bounce from the $1,712 low, with ETH now pushing back toward nearby resistance.

The immediate level sits around $1,833. Reclaiming it would give the latest recovery more weight and begin shifting attention toward the $1,875-$1,880 area, where the next short-term resistance is positioned.

Ethereum has recovered from the $1,712-$1,772 region, with $1,833 now acting as the first level bulls need to reclaim before $1,875-$1,880 comes into view. Source: Trader Symba via X.

Until then, the move remains an early rebound rather than a confirmed reversal. The reaction from the lows is encouraging, but ETH still needs to start converting these nearby resistance levels into support before the lower-timeframe trend can turn more decisively bullish.

ETH/BTC Approaches a Long-Term Accumulation Region

The broader ETH/BTC chart offers a different perspective on the correction. Macro view shows the pair trading back near a long-term support region that has produced major reactions during previous market cycles.

ETH/BTC is returning toward a long-term support region near 0.028 BTC. Source: Trader XO via X.

ETH/BTC is now around the 0.028 area after spending much of the past several years trending lower from its 2021-2022 highs. Rather than looking for additional shorts, the analysis is beginning to shift toward accumulation, with the larger idea centered on building spot exposure before eventually moving into swing longs once momentum confirms.

Trader XO’s chart leaves open the possibility that the final low could take more time to form, with the larger recovery potentially developing through 2027 or 2028. Still, the change in positioning is notable: the focus is moving away from selling rallies and toward identifying where the next macro accumulation phase begins.

Binance ETH Reserves Fall to Their Lowest Level Since 2021

The supply side is also moving in a more constructive direction. CryptoQuant data shared by Cointelegraph shows Ethereum reserves on Binance falling to approximately 2.9 million ETH, worth around $5.3 billion, the lowest level recorded since 2021.

The decline has been substantial. Binance ETH reserves are now roughly 42% lower than they were in July 2025, continuing a broader trend of Ethereum leaving the exchange even while price remains under pressure.

Lower exchange balances do not guarantee an immediate rally, but they reduce the amount of ETH sitting readily available for sale. If demand across retail and institutions begins recovering while reserves continue falling, that tighter liquid supply could become increasingly important for the next larger move.

Ethereum reserves on Binance have fallen to approximately 2.9 million ETH. Source: Cointelegraph via X.

ETH and Global Market Conditions

Ethereum’s weakness is not developing in isolation. Crypto has been trading through a broader risk-off environment, with Bitcoin also under heavy pressure as hotter inflation data, tighter rate expectations, and a stronger dollar weigh on speculative assets. The latest weekly selloff pushed both BTC and ETH sharply lower while leveraged positions were forced out of the market.

That backdrop makes Ethereum’s rebound from the recent lows more meaningful, but also harder to trust too early. ETH still has to contend with weak institutional flows and cautious sentiment across risk assets, so a sustainable recovery will likely need some improvement beyond Ethereum itself. If Bitcoin begins stabilizing and macro pressure eases, the recovery signals already developing around ETH could have more room to play out.

Final Thoughts: Will Panic Selling Stop in Q4 2026?

Ethereum’s latest decline has had many of the characteristics of a market under stress: falling prices, forced liquidations and investors reducing exposure at the same time. That can continue for longer than expected, but it can also create the conditions for a sharper recovery once forced selling begins to fade. Recent reports show substantial long liquidations amplified the downside, rather than the move being driven entirely by a deterioration in Ethereum’s underlying fundamentals.

For the broader Ethereum Price Prediction, the remainder of Q4 may therefore depend less on another immediate bullish breakout and more on whether the market can move beyond this liquidation-heavy phase. title: ChatGPT Wallet vs. Google Gemini: Who Will Lead AI Shopping and Personal Finance?
summary: OpenAI and Google are pushing artificial intelligence deeper into everyday money decisions, but their latest wallet features target two distinct parts of the consumer experience.
content:
Skip to content

OpenAI and Google are pushing artificial intelligence deeper into everyday money decisions, but their latest wallet features target two distinct parts of the consumer experience.

ChatGPT Wallet enables AI agents to complete online purchases with user approval, while Google Gemini uses financial transaction data to deliver personalized spending insights, subscription tracking, and budgeting assistance. Both announcements, made on November 13, 2026, highlight how AI platforms are expanding beyond traditional conversations.

ChatGPT Wallet Brings AI Agents Into Online Shopping

OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that allows its always-on AI agents, known as dots, to complete online purchases on behalf of users. The feature is designed to move AI beyond product research and recommendations by allowing agents to handle checkout through supported websites.

OpenAI’s new feature enables its always-on AI agents, Dots, to complete online purchases securely with explicit user approval for every transaction. Source: ChatGPT via X

The payment process retains user control. Customers first add an eligible payment card to their wallet. When an agent finds a product, users can review the selected items, purchase total, and payment method before approving the transaction through a security check such as Face ID or fingerprint authentication.

Security is central to the system. OpenAI has partnered with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa to use tokenized payments instead of exposing actual card details. Following approval, the payment network generates a temporary substitute containing the information needed to complete the transaction.

This approach prevents the AI agent and merchant from accessing the user’s actual card details. OpenAI also says eligible purchases retain existing card rewards and protections for qualifying disputes.

Mastercard Executive Vice President Sherri Haymond described the objective, saying, “An agent making a purchase should strengthen, not bypass, the trust built into payments.”

ChatGPT Wallet began rolling out on November 13 to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued cards. OpenAI is initially limiting access while it evaluates real-world transactions and works with businesses, banks, and payment providers to improve compatibility.

Google Gemini Adds AI-Powered Personal Finance Insights

Google is approaching AI-powered financial services from a different direction. Its new Google Wallet integration connects spending information to Gemini’s Personal Intelligence feature, allowing the assistant to provide financial guidance based on users’ transaction histories.

Google’s integration of Wallet into Gemini’s Personal Intelligence feature enables AI-driven financial insights using users’ spending data directly within the app. Source: Google via X

US users can connect Google Wallet to Gemini and ask questions about their spending habits by tagging @Google Wallet in conversations. The assistant can generate dynamic charts showing cash flow, asset allocation, and budgets directly within the chat.

Subscription tracking is another feature. Gemini can identify recurring payments across linked accounts and highlight subscriptions whose prices have increased. Users can also review previous spending on categories such as gifts and travel to develop personalized holiday budgets.

Google demonstrated how the feature could support savings planning through a sample request to save $1,000 over three months. Gemini can analyze spending patterns and suggest adjustments, such as reducing dining, rideshare, and subscription expenses.

The integration also supports Plaid, allowing users to connect eligible bank accounts and credit cards to Google Wallet for deeper financial analysis.

Unlike ChatGPT Wallet, however, Google’s feature does not authorize AI-driven purchases or financial transactions. Google emphasizes that Gemini has read-only access to connected account information. As the company explained, the assistant cannot “move, manage, or invest your money.”

Users can also enable or disable the connection through Personal Intelligence settings.

ChatGPT Wallet vs. Google Gemini: Security and Privacy Differences

Both companies are placing user authorization at the center of their financial AI strategies, but their security models serve different purposes.

ChatGPT Wallet focuses on protecting payment credentials during agent-led purchases. Tokenization keeps actual card information away from AI agents and merchants, while biometric approval provides an additional authorization step before checkout.

OpenAI and Google are expanding AI-powered financial services, enabling ChatGPT to facilitate purchases and Gemini to analyze spending and track subscriptions. Source: @ANCrypto_/X

Google Gemini prioritizes controlled access to financial information. Its integration allows the assistant to analyze transaction data without gaining permission to transfer funds or manage investments. Connecting accounts through Plaid is optional, and users retain control over the connection.

The distinction is important. OpenAI is developing a system that can initiate and complete commercial transactions after approval, whereas Google is building an AI assistant that interprets financial activity and helps users make informed decisions.

Both approaches still depend on consumer trust. Payment security, data privacy, accurate recommendations, and transparent authorization will influence how widely people adopt these financial tools.

Who Will Lead AI Shopping and Personal Finance?

The latest developments do not establish a direct winner because ChatGPT Wallet and Google Gemini currently address different needs.

OpenAI has an early advantage in AI shopping by connecting product discovery with payment execution. Its partnerships with established card networks provide an existing payment infrastructure, although merchant compatibility and the limited initial rollout could affect adoption.

Google, meanwhile, is focusing on personalized financial insights. Its integration with Google Wallet and Plaid gives Gemini access to spending information that can support budgeting, subscription monitoring, and savings planning. Its read-only approach also establishes a clear boundary around financial transactions.

Availability is another difference. ChatGPT Wallet initially targets eligible US ChatGPT Pro subscribers, while Google’s Google Wallet integration is rolling out to Gemini app users in the United States across web and mobile.

Ultimately, the two developments represent different directions in the expansion of AI-powered financial services. OpenAI is moving toward agent-led commerce, while Google is strengthening AI-assisted personal finance management.

Their long-term adoption will depend on how reliably these features work, whether users trust AI with sensitive financial information, and how quickly access expands beyond their initial US markets.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Today: $65K Support Under Pressure as Glassnode Maps $60K–$62K Liquidation Cluster
summary: Bitcoin faces renewed selling pressure near $65,000 as weakening demand, negative ETF flows, and underwater investor positions increase downside risks.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin faces renewed selling pressure near $65,000 as weakening demand, negative ETF flows, and underwater investor positions increase downside risks.

Glassnode’s futures liquidation heat map identifies a concentrated cluster of leveraged long positions between $60,000 and $62,000, raising concerns that another decline could trigger forced liquidations.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant data show that large-holder accumulation has failed to offset broader distribution. However, several momentum indicators suggest Bitcoin price is oversold, as its moving-average structure continues to reflect a bearish trend.

Bitcoin Liquidation Heat Map Puts $60K–$62K in Focus

Glassnode’s liquidation heat map highlights a significant concentration of Bitcoin futures long positions between $60,000 and $62,000. These positions are associated with leveraged entries around the August breakout.

The chart highlights a significant concentration of Bitcoin futures long liquidations around $60,000–$62,000, linked to positions opened during the August breakout. Source: Glassndoe/X

Liquidation clusters identify price areas where leveraged traders could face forced position closures. If Bitcoin enters this zone, automatic liquidations could increase selling pressure and accelerate an existing decline.

While the $60,000–$62,000 range is not a confirmed downside target, the concentration of leveraged positions makes it a critical zone to monitor if Bitcoin’s selling pressure intensifies. Following weeks of November selling, traders are watching whether nearby support can hold or whether leveraged positions face another round of liquidations.

Recent Bitcoin Buyers Face Unrealized Losses

CryptoQuant reports that Bitcoin’s 24% decline has pushed recent buyers into negative unrealized returns. Their unrealized profits have fallen from approximately 35% in September to -15%, with an estimated on-chain cost basis of $80,300 against market prices near $65,000.

Bitcoin’s 24% decline has pushed recent buyers into losses, with unrealized returns falling from +35% in September to -15% as their $80,300 cost basis exceeds current prices near $65,000. Source: CryptoQuant/X

Wallet activity also reveals contrasting behavior among large holders. Addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have accumulated approximately 47,000 BTC. However, wallets holding between 10 and 1,000 BTC have reduced their balances by around 65,000 BTC.

Negative US spot Bitcoin ETF flows and 30-day apparent demand of approximately -284,000 BTC add to the pressure. These figures suggest that accumulation among the largest holders has not been sufficient to offset broader distribution and weak market demand.

CryptoQuant identifies $68,700–$76,000 as an important resistance range. On the downside, $63,000 is a nearby support reference, while Bitcoin’s realized price near $53,800 represents a deeper on-chain level to monitor.

Bitcoin | Expanded Flat or Zigzag?

Elliott Wave analyst Mehdi_Abbasi_EWP identifies two possible interpretations of Bitcoin’s broader correction.

Bitcoin previously declined from $126,272 to approximately $57,870 before recovering toward $87,330. The latest downturn has created uncertainty over whether the recovery completed a corrective pattern or represented the first phase of a larger structure.

Bitcoin has developed a five-wave bearish Elliott Wave structure following its peak at $126,272. Source: Mehdi_Abbasi_EWP/TradingView

Scenario 1: Expanded Flat

Under the Expanded Flat interpretation, the recovery toward $87,330 may have completed Waves A and B, with the current decline beginning Wave C.

A five-wave bearish structure in the ongoing decline would support this scenario. A break below $57,870 would provide further confirmation.

The analyst identifies $45,863 and $34,615 as potential downside targets if this structure develops.

Scenario 2: Zigzag

The alternative interpretation views the advance from $57,870 to $87,330 as Wave A of a larger Zigzag correction.

Under this scenario, the current decline represents Wave B, leaving room for another corrective recovery before Wave C begins. The $95,000–$96,000 region, corresponding to the 38.2%–61.8% Fibonacci retracement zone, is an area to watch if buyers regain control.

However, the subsequent Wave C could still produce another decline, with $34,615 remaining a potential downside target.

The Structural Difference Between the Two Scenarios

The main distinction concerns whether the advance toward $87,330 completed an Expanded Flat’s corrective structure or represented the first wave of a larger Zigzag.

The internal wave structure and price behavior around $57,870 will help determine which interpretation is more consistent with market developments. Neither scenario is confirmed at this stage.

Bitcoin Technical Analysis: Oversold Signals Emerge Amid Bearish Momentum

Bitcoin trades near $65,458 in the supplied BITSTAMP technical snapshot, down approximately 2.49% in the latest session.

The overall technical summary shows a Sell signal, with 14 sell readings, five neutral, and seven buy signals. Moving averages carry a Strong Sell designation, while oscillators lean toward Buy as several momentum indicators enter oversold territory.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands at 25, while the Stochastic %K is at 9 and the Commodity Channel Index (CCI) reads -215. These levels indicate substantial selling pressure and leave room for a potential short-term rebound.

However, the MACD remains negative at -3,499, while the Average Directional Index (ADX) stands at 31, indicating an established trend. The broader technical structure therefore remains bearish despite oversold readings.

Nearly all major moving averages sit above Bitcoin’s current price. The 10-day EMA is around $70,783, the 20-day EMA at $73,926, and the 50-day EMA near $77,094. The 200-day EMA stands at approximately $76,035.

These averages could create successive resistance barriers during a recovery. Bitcoin would need to reclaim the $70,000–$73,000 region before challenging higher levels.

Key Levels to Watch

Classic pivot calculations identify $80,274 as the central pivot, with resistance at $84,375, $91,321, and $102,367.

On the downside, support levels stand at:

  • $73,329: First support
  • $69,227: Second support
  • $58,181: Third support

These levels complement the $63,000 support identified by CryptoQuant. A sustained breakdown could expose Bitcoin to the previous low near $57,870 and the realized price around $53,800.

Bitcoin Price Outlook: Will $65K Hold or Will Sellers Target $60K?

Bitcoin’s immediate outlook depends on whether buyers can defend the $63,000–$65,000 region and restore demand. Glassnode’s $60,000–$62,000 liquidation cluster highlights the potential for additional volatility if selling accelerates.

On the upside, $68,700 is an important initial resistance, followed by the broader $70,000–$76,000 region. Oversold momentum indicators could support a temporary recovery, but stronger spot demand and improved ETF flows would be necessary to challenge the broader bearish structure.

For now, weak demand, negative momentum, and persistent distribution keep downside risks elevated. Bitcoin’s reaction around nearby support levels will help determine whether the latest decline stabilizes or develops into another leg lower.

AI has become the most frequently cited financial-stability risk in a survey published with the Federal Reserve’s latest report, bringing the technology boom’s financing and market connections into sharper focus.

The November 13 Financial Stability Report says 87% of 23 market contacts surveyed in September and October cited AI, compared with 50% of 20 contacts in the spring. The concerns span valuations, cyber events and complicated financing arrangements.

For crypto investors, the significance lies in those channels of transmission. A shock does not need to originate inside Bitcoin to influence the people, lenders and trading infrastructure around it.

What the Fed AI risk figure actually measures

The report describes the survey box as a summary of respondents’ views. It says those views “should not be interpreted as representing the views of the Federal Reserve Board.”

That distinction prevents an eye-catching statistic becoming something it is not. An 87% response rate for a particular concern is not an 87% chance of a crisis, and the small sample is not a representative poll of all investors.

The collection period also matters. The answers were gathered before November’s latest market and corporate developments. They show concerns already present among financial professionals, rather than a measured reaction to the most recent headlines.

These are different survey groups at different times. The increase is a useful change in reported concern, but it cannot establish how each individual respondent changed their mind.

The financing question is bigger than whether AI works

A separate section of the report puts advanced-computing-related debt issuance above $680 billion by October 2026, compared with $130 billion in all of 2023. The figures concern issuance, rather than the same-period growth rate or the total value of the AI industry.

The investment question is therefore broader than model quality. A useful technology can attract spending that is poorly timed, too expensive or financed on terms that leave little room for disappointment. Strong demand and weak investment returns can coexist.

Consider a data-centre project that must pay lenders before customers deliver the expected cash. If deployment is delayed, the financing cost continues. A contract can support confidence in eventual demand while still leaving a cash-flow problem in the intervening months.

BNC’s CoreWeave earnings analysis offered a company-level example: rising revenue alongside substantial interest expense. The relevance is the relationship between growth and funding costs, rather than a claim that one company’s results establish a system-wide problem.

Why a technology shock can reach unrelated assets

One potential route is portfolio rebalancing. An investor facing losses in one position may reduce another to raise cash or meet a risk limit. That sale says something about the investor’s balance sheet, but not necessarily about the second asset’s fundamental prospects.

Another route is credit. If lenders reassess the risk of ambitious infrastructure projects, the cost or availability of financing can change. Companies dependent on fresh funding are more exposed to that adjustment than firms able to finance operations from existing cash generation.

For Bitcoin, those are reasons to monitor the broader financial setting. They are not proof that every AI stock decline must trigger a cryptocurrency sell-off. The size of the connection depends on who holds the positions, how they are financed and what other buyers are prepared to absorb.

Cyber risk is also a market-functioning issue

The Fed’s May financial-stability discussion had already described how attacks or software failures at financial institutions and third-party providers can impair services, weaken confidence and propagate through interconnected systems. The concern predates the latest survey.

That is particularly relevant to markets whose users depend on exchanges, custodians, cloud services and payment routes. A blockchain continuing to produce blocks does not ensure that every customer can reach an account, obtain a price or transfer money through an intermediary.

The practical question is where a critical dependency sits. If several firms rely on the same service, a disruption can reach them simultaneously. Resilience depends partly on alternatives, recovery arrangements and the ability to operate while one link is unavailable.

What investors should look for next

More useful evidence than another general warning would be clearer disclosure of borrowing terms, guarantees, customer concentration and the gap between construction spending and operating cash flow. Those details make it possible to judge who can withstand a disappointing quarter.

On the market side, distinguish a broad reduction in risk from an asset-specific reassessment. Prices, financing conditions and actual fund flows can help test that distinction when compared over matching periods. A correlation observed during one stressful week is not a permanent law.

The new survey does not settle whether AI is overvalued or predict the next crisis. It establishes that market contacts increasingly see the boom as a financial question as well as a technological one. For crypto readers, following the money and the dependencies may now be as useful as following the models.
